author: Garoozies
text:
6- Good.
Good thing I have no followers that read my reviews otherwise posting this would require some real bravery. I picked this game up anticipating a 10/10 experience. Anticipating to be swept off my feet. And that I was, in moments. But the truth is that this game is not a 10/10 experience. There are things about it that are perfect. It’s a technical marvel, and its commitment to realism and simulation are impressive even if selectively applied. The narrative is excellent as well, but, not perfect either. Arthur is a richly deep character with nuance of purpose and morals. Unraveling him beat by beat as the Van Der Linde gang comes undone is a beautiful exploration of the characters and setting. But the gameplay is honestly weak and formulaic. Gunfights all play out nigh identically. The cycle of find character, initiate cutscene, ride to location, gunfight, cutscene, mission end- cannot seriously be the best and only mission structure Rockstar can come up with? Gunfights are weak, the expository horse rides are incredibly long and repetitious even if the dialogue is interesting. I played RDR and 2 back to back and honestly find little outside of the technical presentation to have been improved. When I was simply progressing the story I found myself on the border of disliking the game. But, as fans will quickly point out, this is an open world game meant to be explored and experienced. So about halfway through I pivoted, slowed down, and explored. The game is better enjoyed this way and it brought me back to liking the game. But, compared to the greatest open worlds I’ve experienced, RDR2 lacks the same extrinsic motivation that keeps me in it. Hunting for perfect pelts is enjoyable in small bursts between missions and there’s a lot of lore tidbits and flourishes that make the world incredibly realistic and immersive. Ultimately, this game is great. Meaning it deserves praises, it deserves attention, and it deserves to be many people’s favorite game.

author: kauezimCRITC
text: **Red Dead Redemption 2 – Uma obra-prima que redefiniu o padrão da indústria**Red Dead Redemption 2 não é apenas um jogo. É uma demonstração do que acontece quando uma empresa decide priorizar qualidade, atenção aos detalhes e visão artística acima da pressa. Em uma indústria onde muitos lançamentos chegam incompletos, dependem de atualizações no primeiro dia e frequentemente são construídos em torno de microtransações, Red Dead Redemption 2 mostra que ainda é possível criar uma experiência completa, extremamente polida e memorável.O primeiro aspecto que impressiona é o nível de detalhes. Quase tudo no mundo reage ao jogador de maneira natural. Os NPCs possuem rotinas próprias, lembram de determinadas ações, conversam entre si e fazem o mundo parecer vivo. Os animais não existem apenas como decoração: cada espécie possui comportamentos específicos, cadeias alimentares e reações diferentes ao ambiente. O clima muda de forma dinâmica, a vegetação responde ao vento, a lama acumula nas roupas e os cavalos possuem animações e comportamentos únicos. São milhares de pequenos detalhes que, individualmente, parecem simples, mas juntos criam um nível de imersão raramente visto.A narrativa também está entre as melhores já produzidas nos videogames. Arthur Morgan é um dos protagonistas mais bem escritos da história da mídia. Sua jornada mostra conflitos internos, lealdade, arrependimento, amizade e redenção de uma maneira extremamente humana. O roteiro não depende apenas de grandes explosões ou reviravoltas; ele conquista o jogador através da construção gradual dos personagens e das relações entre eles. O resultado é uma história emocional que permanece na memória muito tempo depois dos créditos finais.Tecnicamente, Red Dead Redemption 2 também impressiona. Os gráficos continuam competitivos mesmo anos após o lançamento. A iluminação, a física, as animações faciais, a captura de movimentos, o design sonoro e a trilha sonora trabalham em conjunto para criar uma experiência cinematográfica. Cada cidade possui identidade própria, cada região apresenta fauna, flora e arquitetura distintas, e a exploração constantemente recompensa a curiosidade do jogador.Outro ponto que merece destaque é a liberdade oferecida. O jogador pode seguir a campanha principal, caçar animais lendários, explorar cavernas, resolver mistérios, encontrar eventos aleatórios, ajudar desconhecidos, cometer crimes ou simplesmente cavalgar observando o pôr do sol. Poucos jogos conseguem fazer o mundo aberto parecer tão vivo e interessante sem depender de centenas de marcadores artificiais no **** Dead Redemption 2 também representa um contraste em relação a muitos problemas atuais da indústria. Nos últimos anos, diversos jogos passaram a ser lançados com desempenho ruim, conteúdo cortado para futuras expansões, excesso de monetização e falta de polimento. Esse cenário gerou frustração entre muitos jogadores. Nesse contexto, Red Dead Redemption 2 demonstra que ainda existe espaço para produções extremamente ambiciosas, nas quais o foco principal é entregar um produto completo e de alta **** entanto, é importante fazer uma distinção. A qualidade extraordinária do jogo não significa que qualquer método utilizado durante seu desenvolvimento deva ser considerado positivo. Há relatos públicos de longas jornadas de trabalho durante parte da produção. É perfeitamente possível admirar o resultado final e reconhecer a dedicação da equipe sem concluir que condições excessivas de trabalho sejam desejáveis. O mérito principal pertence ao enorme talento de milhares de artistas, programadores, roteiristas, designers, engenheiros, músicos e demais profissionais **** Dead Redemption 2 elevou o padrão da indústria porque mostrou que videogames podem alcançar um nível artístico comparável ao do cinema e da literatura, sem abandonar a diversão característica do meio. Seu legado influencia desenvolvedores do mundo inteiro e continua servindo como referência em narrativa, construção de mundo, tecnologia e direção **** tudo isso, Red Dead Redemption 2 merece ser lembrado como uma das maiores obras da história dos videogames. Não porque seja perfeito — nenhum jogo é —, mas porque estabelece um padrão de excelência que poucos conseguiram alcançar. Ele desafia outras empresas a investirem em qualidade, inovação e respeito pelo jogador. Em uma época em que muitos lançamentos decepcionam por chegarem inacabados ou priorizarem modelos de monetização acima da experiência, Red Dead Redemption 2 permanece como um exemplo de que ambição, talento e atenção aos detalhes podem produzir algo verdadeiramente extraordinário. É um jogo que não apenas diverte, mas também inspira, emociona e demonstra até onde a indústria dos videogames é capaz de chegar quando busca excelência.

author: Fayaaz
text:
I went into Red Dead Redemption 2 expecting a fun cowboy simulator, and I came out of it convinced it’s the absolute best game ever created. 

Rockstar really built a world that feels completely alive, though it definitely knows how to catch you off guard. The realism in this game is wild, especially when it comes to your horse. The game forces you to actually bond with your steed, to the point where I spent an embarrassing amount of time brushing it, patting it, and feeding it carrots just to max out that bonding level. You genuinely start to care about that digital animal. Beyond the horses, the sheer amount of "other stuff" to do is staggering. You can easily lose fifty hours just hunting legendary animals, upgrading the camp ledger, playing poker in Saint Denis, or accidentally punching a random NPC because you pressed the wrong button. The attention to detail is so intense that even the weather affects how your character performs.

But the real danger is how attached you get to the Van der Linde gang. The writing is so good that when things start going downhill, it hits hard. Sean was my boy—my absolute favorite character in the camp—so his sudden exit in Rhodes left my jaw completely on the floor. It was a brutal reminder of how high the stakes are. And Arthur’s slow-burn journey and ultimate demise? It’s easily one of the most tragic, beautifully written arcs in media history. Watching the camp slowly fall apart under the pressure just kept me glued to the screen.

At the end of the day, the highs are unmatched and the tragic moments only prove how masterpiece-tier the storytelling is. If you haven't played it yet, drop everything and buy it immediately. It’s a flawless experience that everyone needs to try at least once. To me this IS the best game I have ever played!

author: Mythjohn
text: First off I gotta say I actually uninstalled this game and reinstalled it later. That snowy part at the very beginning is just way too slow and honestly it was so boring I couldn't handle it back then and just dropped it. When I installed it the second time it didn't bother me as much but you still get into the story way too slowly man. Once you get past the train mission and move the camp the game suddenly opens up and feels way better. You start seeing different people outside the camp there aren't towns everywhere on the map just in specific spots but the npcs there aren't just placed to stand around. They actually have things to do and it feels like they genuinely live there. The missions are already legendary and the story flow is so good I really liked the design of Saint Denis. There was one thing driving me crazy early on though I kept thinking why the hell is this guy moving so slowly the character felt super clunky. Then I realized something when controlling Arthur it actually feels like I am the one walking in real life. After a while I honestly started to love that heavy clunky feeling. The gunfights are just absolutely perfect I have never seen gunplay this satisfying in any other game. The melee animations are rock solid too when you stab someone with a knife you really feel the weight of it since the whole point of the game is to make everything feel real anyway. Story wise I genuinely ended up loving Arthur I didn't really vibe with him at first but the more I played the more attached I got to the dude and Sadie s character arc was really good too. I especially gotta point out that they pulled off something other devs usually fail at which is connecting the story to the first game so perfectly they explain everything one by one we even get to see that famous house being built. The revenge part at the end didn't feel super satisfying to me but it still isn't bad this game is a straight up masterpiece and hands down deserves a 9.6/10

author: Bitt03
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 tells one of the best stories in gaming, and Arthur Morgan is a protagonist I will remember for a very long time. His journey is emotional, well-written, and carries the entire experience from beginning to end. The game's world is also incredibly immersive, filled with attention to detail that few other titles can match. However, if the story is taken out of the equation, the gameplay itself is fairly average. Many mechanics feel slow and repetitive, and the mission design rarely offers much freedom. Despite that, the combination of a memorable narrative and a beautifully crafted world makes Red Dead Redemption 2 an excellent game overall.

author: sauddiarabia
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is a staggering achievement in digital storytelling, functioning less like a traditional video game and more like a living, breathing historical epic that demands total immersion. Set at the sunset of the outlaw era in 1899, the narrative follows Arthur Morgan, a man caught between his unwavering loyalty to the Van der Linde gang and the encroaching march of modern civilization. What sets this experience apart is its uncompromising commitment to realism; every action, from the rhythmic cleaning of a sidearm to the physical weight of Arthur’s movement through thick mud, is rendered with meticulous detail that creates a profound sense of presence. The world itself is a technical marvel, featuring an ecosystem where predators hunt in the brush and dynamic weather systems transform the sprawling landscapes from the snow-capped peaks of the Grizzlies to the humid, industrial grit of Saint Denis. This deliberate pacing might challenge those seeking instant gratification, but it serves a greater purpose: it forces a connection between the player and the environment, turning simple acts like grooming a horse or sitting by a campfire into moments of genuine reflection. It is a haunting, beautiful tragedy that explores themes of redemption, the cost of loyalty, and the inevitable passage of time, ultimately standing as one of the most sophisticated and emotionally resonant works in the medium.

author: Jowyyy
text:
I have heard how famous “Red Dead Redemption 2” is for a very long while. Some of my friends praise it for the storytelling and how Rockstar writes their characters. Ridiculously, the thing that successfully hooks me to this game is how realistic the graphic is, as I have heard people talk about it for years and until now. So, when the game was on sale, I decided to buy it and find it out myself.

When I first entered the game, I was a little confused since all I saw was just snow. But even only the first chapter proves to me enough why the game is admired by its realistic graphics. I would consider it ‘insane’ for a game that was released 8-7 years ago. No wonder that the game is immersive; Snow leaves trail when you drive a wagon. Animals act the exact way they live in the woods. I now understand that what I have heard before is all true, as well as I understand why they require around 100 GB.

The music and ambience go pretty well with the visual as well, a perfect mix of The Wild West aesthetic, a country side, and a calming nature. UI designs match the game’s aesthetic and the gameplay UI is very neat, as the game tries to be immersive as much as possible. Not to mention how much effort the actors and actresses put into their given roles. I call them ‘actors and actresses’ because the game does use motion and performance capture, so not only Rockstar hired them to voice the characters, but to ‘perform’ their actions as well.

Even though I would consider this a decent game, there’s some flaw in it as well. Although the game is immersive and gives you serenity, some people may find it boring as the game has a very slow-paced progression. You play as Arthur, traveling by horse from towns to towns to clear both main quests and side quests, hunt animals and fish, only to fill the donation jar and upgrade stuff in your camp, some that are not even that useful. People may find that the game loop is not that rewarding, so it’s understandable why people could say it’s tedious for a vast scale of the game.

Nevertheless, I would still recommend this game, especially for people who love open world games and want to take a break from online games and enjoy a moment of peace in offline games instead. If you love to find interesting secrets or details, then you must try it for yourself. It might feel slow at the very start, but once you get used to being Arthur, then I’m sure you will slowly feel the very same way as him and even understand his perspective. In the end, his understanding of the world might uplift your life. At that moment, you will truly understand, that it’s never too late for one’s redemption.

author: Etxeberra
text:
Todos sabemos de la suprema calidad de este juego, tanto en lo técnico como en lo jugable. Aunque han habido cosas en esto último que para mi gusto, le han impedido alcanzar la excelencia:

1) el gunplay. No es satisfactorio que no sea totalmente responsiva, ya que es fácil que el personaje "se cubra" del lado expuesto de la cobertura. Este es un fallo que se presenta en coberturas angostas como árboles, situación que no es rápidamente corregible moviendo el personaje. 

2) el savegame: ¿necesitas guardar en medio de una misión o simplemente en medio de un combate? No puedes. Si sales del juego en estos casos, tendrás que volver a activar la misión, que podrá significar tener que desplazarse al lugar.

3) gestión de actividades. Acceder fácilmente una tarea en concreto en el diario es una tarea en sí misma, pues queda perdida en medio de otros elementos que se registran.

4) zonas restringidas en el mapa. Hay una zona en particular no accesible hasta bien avanzada la historia y su restricción es forzada.

5) los NPC tienen rutinas, pero no son responsivos. Sólo lo hacen aquellos vinculados a eventos aleatorios.

6) el sistema de reputación es generalista, pues a pesar de cometer actos en zonas reducidas, la reputación se aplica hasta en poblados no conocidos.

7) el sigilo. La peor implementación en el gameplay porque simplemente no funciona. La muestra es que estando agazapados de noche, de repente un personaje a varios metros de distancia y automáticamente todos los enemigos cercanos también lo hacen. 

8) no hay libertad de ejecución de las misiones. Tienen que hacerse como el juego lo tiene programado.

9) a propósito de las misiones, una vez se active una, tiene que hacerse de inmediato. No se pueden hacer otras cosas como ejecutar una inspección previa, o simplemente hacer otras tareas.

author: arthurfedaisi
text: A Masterpiece of Modern Game Design: A Critical Appreciation of Red Dead Redemption 2**In an era where the video game industry often prioritizes spectacle over substance, *Red Dead Redemption 2* stands as a rare and remarkable exception. Developed by Rockstar Games, this title transcends the conventional boundaries of interactive entertainment, delivering an experience that is as emotionally profound as it is technically impressive. From its meticulously crafted world to its deeply human narrative, the game represents a pinnacle of artistic achievement within the **** the heart of *Red Dead Redemption 2* lies its narrative, a slow-burning yet deeply immersive story centered on the Van der Linde gang and its internal struggles. Unlike many modern titles that rely on constant action to maintain engagement, the game embraces patience and subtlety. The protagonist, Arthur Morgan, is portrayed with extraordinary depth, evolving from a hardened outlaw into a reflective and morally complex individual. This transformation is not forced upon the player but emerges organically through choices, interactions, and the passage of time. Such character development is rarely seen in video games, placing the narrative on par with high-quality cinema and literature.Equally impressive is the game’s open world, which is arguably one of the most detailed ever created. Every corner of the environment feels alive, from bustling towns to quiet, untouched wilderness. The ecosystem operates with a sense of realism that enhances immersion; wildlife behaves naturally, NPCs follow daily routines, and even minor interactions contribute to the world’s authenticity. This level of detail is not merely aesthetic but functional, encouraging players to engage with the environment in meaningful ways rather than treating it as a passive backdrop.Technically, the game is a masterpiece. The visual fidelity, lighting systems, and environmental design work in harmony to create breathtaking landscapes that rival real-world photography. Combined with a carefully composed soundtrack and exceptional voice acting, the result is an audiovisual experience that consistently reinforces the game’s emotional tone. The attention to detail extends to animation and physics, where even the smallest movements feel deliberate and grounded.However, what truly sets *Red Dead Redemption 2* apart is its willingness to challenge the player. Its deliberate pacing, often criticized by some, is in fact a strength. By slowing down the experience, the game invites players to reflect on its themes of loyalty, morality, and the inevitability of change. It resists the instant gratification model that dominates the industry, instead offering a more contemplative and rewarding **** conclusion, *Red Dead Redemption 2* is not merely a video game but a work of art. It demonstrates what the medium is capable of when developers prioritize depth, authenticity, and emotional resonance. While it may not appeal to every player due to its pacing and complexity, for those willing to engage with it fully, the experience is unparalleled. It is, without question, one of the greatest achievements in the history of gaming.

author: Harrsshallll
text: One thing stands out right away in Red Dead Redemption 2 the world breathes on its own Step into it and you begin to notice how every detail carries weight Mountains rise without warning forests stretch farther than expected and rivers twist through land that seems to remember footsteps Towns hum with routines untouched by your arrival Rain comes when least expected animals move with purpose and people glance at you as if you matter but are not special Completing tasks matters less than paying attention Staying quiet watching and walking long distances reveal what lies beneath The game becomes richer when you slow down even though it never tells you to The storytelling is where the game truly stands out Arthur Morgan ranks among the finest characters in gaming He feels human and raw carrying a weight that lingers long after moments pass Emotion runs through everything he does Personal battles shape how he moves forward Growth appears slowly and quietly without fanfare Doubt creeps in often shaping his choices His struggles are not grand but quiet and real The gang around him feels alive Bonds form not from duty but from shared history Each member acts with motivations that are not immediately clear Motives unfold when least expected Conversations never sound rehearsed Words land because they feel lived in Voices carry meaning beyond simple dialogue Performances pull you deeper into the experience Moments stay with you not because they shock but because they matter What also stands out is how carefully everything is crafted Almost every activity invites interaction You can chase wildlife cast a fishing line talk with strangers or simply ride your horse across open fields The game encourages you to move at its own pace and notice what surrounds you Snow keeps tracks where animals walk Wildlife behaves realistically and towns change and grow over time These small touches add depth without drawing attention to themselves Gameplay feels smooth and engaging Gunfights are intense grounded and satisfying Exploration feels calm and almost peaceful Music blends into every moment naturally At sunset while riding horseback the soundtrack quietly supports the atmosphere During emotional story moments the music rises just enough to enhance the scene Each note feels perfectly placed never overwhelming and never missing Beyond gameplay Red Dead Redemption 2 stands as a remarkable achievement that reshapes storytelling in games Its depth lingers long after the final scene World details pull you in without forcing your attention making everything feel natural rather than staged Emotion builds slowly through observation instead of speeches Few games achieve this level of immersion while staying grounded Time spent in this world does not fade quickly it settles and stays with you long after you leave

author: AliErdogaaan
text:
.​In my opinion, the greatest achievement of Red Dead Redemption 2 was exactly this: making the player feel that solitude. When you add the magnificent nature, the atmosphere of cities transforming during the Industrial Revolution, loyalty, and action to this theme, you get a masterpiece that players divide into "before RDR2" and "after RDR2."​From Arthur Morgan's Journal:​"The world has always seemed dark and cruel to me."​...​"Saint Denis is a depressive place that shows you the only thing worse than a man is more men."​After getting used to the speed of modern games, RDR2's heavy controls felt slow at first. However, Rockstar Games has set the bar so high that the game eventually makes you feel that Arthur Morgan's heavy steps are actually meant to reflect the gravity of the story and the realism of the atmosphere.​Set in 1899, a prequel to RDR1, we witness the survival struggle of the Dutch van der Linde gang in an era where "civilization" (central government and police) is slowly destroying the Wild West—or more accurately, trying to end the era of outlaws and apply the law to everyone. Our primary goal isn't just revenge (though it seems so at first); it’s the step-by-step dissolution of a small community/family that cannot adapt to the changing world, and one man’s (Arthur) search for Redemption.​This quote perfectly summarizes my feelings:​"You play some games and they end; you live RDR2, and it continues to live with you."​Comparing it to other successful titles I've played recently, like Days Gone and The Last of Us Part 1 & 2, the tension of "survival" in those games gives way to a feeling of "living" here. In Days Gone, you worry about running out of gas; here, you pet, brush, and feed your horse carrots so it doesn't get tired. The gunplay might not be as sharp as TLOU 2, but using early 19th-century weapons and loading bullets one by one were details that reflected the atmosphere and took realism to the next level.​I had the chance to play RDR2 at the highest resolution, just like Days Gone and TLOU, and I believe that fine details—like the light filtering through the trees at sunset or the fog settling in the valley—take this game to a whole different level.​Regarding the music: "See the Fire in Your Eyes" isn't just background music; it’s a reflection of Arthur’s inner world. When you set out on a long road with your horse and those subtle melodies kick in, you feel the loneliness down to your bones.​Ultimately, Red Dead Redemption 2 is like a heavy novel for me—one that successfully made me feel a completely different world and left me grieving as if I had lost a real friend at its finale.​Score: 9.5 / 10​ 
Arthur’s Tuberculosis: His slow decline, coughing fits, and the light fading from his eyes were heartbreaking. Rockstar gave us a mortal human, not a superhero. Arthur telling the nun at the station, "I guess... I'm afraid," is one of the best performances in gaming history.​At the end, when Arthur’s horse dies and he stops in the middle **** to say "Thank you" to his horse... what a scene. When "That's the Way It Is" started playing, I couldn't stop my eyes from tearing up.​The final fight with Micah, crawling towards the gun, Dutch’s final look before walking away... Arthur taking his last breath against the sunrise and the "May I Stand Unshaken" farewell was more peaceful than Joel’s death but much more wounding.​The "House Building Song" section with John Marston felt like medicine after all that pain.​And amidst all that drama, there's that crazy man shouting, "Gavin! Has anyone seen Gavin?!" in every corner of the map.​The "Night Folk" in the Lemoyne swamps are pure horror material. You see someone hanging from a tree in the dead of night, you dismount, and suddenly "psikopatlar" (psychopaths) rush you silently out of the fog.​Marko Dragic and his robot... they tucked a Tesla-style sci-fi story into a Western game and it fit perfectly. Finding the robot alone on top of a mountain was strangely melancholy.​The Epilogue lasts nearly 5 hours. We witness John learning ranch life.​Arthur’s Journal Entry: "I did it for Abigail and Jack, of course... but I guess I also did it for Marston. The bastard grew on me... he's not as dumb as he used to be, and maybe he can have the luck that didn't come my way."​The Mount Hagen fight was spectacular in terms of action. I wish it were longer.​The story that began in the mountains of Colter ended in the mountains of Hagen.​The credits scenes were beautiful: Abigail and John’s wedding, Charles leaving for Canada, Sadie for South America, the police finding Beecher’s Hope, and Mary Linton visiting Arthur’s grave.

He slowly grows on you, and by the end, he feels like one of the best-written characters in gaming. I also loved how the honor system actually matters, changing dialogue, scenes, and even the ending. It makes your choices feel **** graphics and views on PC are insane, and the freedom the game gives you is amazing. You can explore, hunt, cause chaos, or just ride around and take in the world. Even the bounty system adds to the immersion.That said, the game isn’t perfect. Movement can feel slow and clunky at times, some missions are too restrictive for a game that gives you so much freedom outside them, and the pacing can be very slow, especially in the beginning. But honestly, none of that stopped me from loving **** me, this is Rockstar at its absolute best.

text:
Bir oyun herkes tarafından sevilmeyebilir. Oynayan kişiye hitap etmemiştir ve oyuncu daha fazla vaktini ayırmak istemez. Oyunun ilerleyen bölümleri için merak duygusunu yitirmiştir. Tamam, onu anlarım. Lakin Red Dead Redemption 2'ye yapılan asıl ayıp, oyunun barındırdığı hikaye ve içeriklerden habersizce yapılan kötü eleştiriler. Oyunun sadece ana hikayesinden gidenler ya da uzun süren at kullanım süresinden yakınanlar, oyunun içerisinde bulunan yan hikayelerin çoğundan habersizce gömüyor oyunu. Günümüz oyunların bize ezberlettiği ya da zorunda bıraktığı formüllerin çok dışında bir oynanış sunuyor Rdr2. O dünyada karşınıza çıkabilecek hiçbir unsur gözünüze sokulmuyor, oyuncu görsün diye gereksiz çabalara girmiyor. Gerçek hayat gibi, sizin gidip araştırmanız veya denk gelip görmeniz gerekiyor. Yoksa nereden bileceksiniz ki etrafınızdaki yaşanan olayları yada yaşayanların hikayelerini? Nereden bileceksiniz; Agnes Dowd'u? "Korkak" savaş kahramanını? Ayağını kaybeden buz patencisini? İntihar eden tiyatro sanatçısını? Donmuş çifti? Zaman yolcusunu? "şapşal" aşık kardeşleri? Uzaylı kampını? "Tuhaf" adamı? Çılgın bilim insanını? Deli rahibi? Vampir adamı? Saint Denis mezarlığındaki hayaleti? Kurt adamı? Robotik Frankenstein'ı? Ormanların kralını? Mağara şeytanını? Mutant deneylerini? Kaçak sirk hayvanlarını? Halk önünde yapılan cani deneyi ve aklıma şimdilik daha fazlasının gelmediği onca karakter olayları yada hikayeleri?

Sadece ana hikayeden gidilmez, keşfe dayalı hikayelere açık olunursa oyunun sizde bırakacağı etki çok daha büyük olur. 

Saygılar!

author: Jeffhim
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2 não é apenas um jogo, é uma simulação de vida no Velho Oeste que redefine o que esperamos de fidelidade técnica e profundidade emocional na indústria.
 A jornada de Arthur Morgan é, sem dúvida, uma das melhores histórias já escritas para qualquer mídia. O desenvolvimento de personagens e o peso das escolhas criam uma conexão emocional raramente vista em outros títulos.​
A atenção aos detalhes da Rockstar é obsessiva. Desde o comportamento dos animais até a interação com NPCs, tudo parece orgânico. O mundo não gira em torno de você; ele existe de forma independente, o que torna a exploração fascinante.​Realismo e Ritmo: O jogo exige paciência e entrega uma experiência "visceral". O peso dos movimentos, o sistema de caça e a manutenção das armas trazem uma camada de realismo que faz você se sentir realmente dentro daquele período histórico.​
Ele virou um padrão de gráficos e física, o jogo tem a capacidade de criar momentos únicos através de encontros aleatórios, fazendo com que cada jogador tenha uma história diferente para contar.​
Um épico técnico e emocional. RDR2 é a prova de que videogames podem ser a forma mais elevada de arte.

author: Cernix
text:
Comment ce jeu a perdu le GOTY déjà ? Je suis peut-être biaisé car je n'ai pas aimé God of War (a ajouter à la liste des licences acclamées que je n'aime pas). Mais pour moi c'est une évidence que RDR2 marquera durablement le jeu vidéo. Difficile d'imaginer, après la fin de RDR1, qu'on me ferait autant aimé un autre personnage de cowboy que John Marston, et pourtant bien que plus long à s'installer (durée du jeu oblige je suppose) Arthur Morgan restera, je pense, l'un des personnage les plus complexe et attachant du jeu vidéo. Au même titre que beaucoup des personnages du jeu d'ailleurs. Comme son prédécesseur, RDR2 brille par sa narration, ses dialogues et comme susmentionné ses personnages mais aussi, sa variété de gameplay et son monde ouvert . Cela dit, il en garde quelques défauts. Des gameplays variés mais peu profonds, s'approchant sur certaines missions un peu trop du film interactif à mon goût. Des mécaniques parfois mal intégrées à la boucle de gameplay les transformant plus un corvées qu'autre chose (la chasse, la pêche notamment). Mais surtout des contrôles régulièrement aux fraises (plus que le 1er pour le coup), et des à-côtés pas toujours franchement intéressants (les collectables et défis principalement). Un défaut qui n'a pas été hérité du 1er en revanche : les graphismes, le jeu est encore magnifique aujourd'hui (malgré quelques bugs de lumières) et le motion capture a fait des miracles.
Red Dead Redemption 2 est une épopée incroyable qui vous fera passer par un large spectre d'émotions, inattendues pour certaines. Passez les quelques premières  heures de jeu qui peuvent sembler un peu lente et intimidante, vous ne le regretterez pas.

author: Pombo2011
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 é uma obra-prima que vai muito além de um simples jogo de mundo aberto. A Rockstar entrega um dos universos mais vivos e detalhados já criados, onde cada NPC, cada paisagem e cada pequeno evento contribuem para uma imersão absurda. A narrativa é emocionalmente pesada, madura e extremamente bem escrita, fazendo o jogador se importar de verdade com Arthur Morgan e o destino da gangue. O ritmo pode parecer lento para alguns, mas isso só fortalece a ambientação e o peso das escolhas. O combate é sólido, a trilha sonora é impecável e o cuidado com detalhes é algo raramente visto na indústria. RDR2 não tenta agradar todo mundo — ele conta sua história do jeito que precisa ser contada, e faz isso com excelência. Um jogo marcante, memorável e facilmente um dos melhores já feitos.

author: JaviManu
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 es una obra maestra sin discusión. Todo en este juego está cuidado al detalle: desde la historia profundamente humana y emocional, hasta la construcción de un mundo abierto que se siente vivo, respirando y reaccionando a cada acción del jugador. Arthur Morgan y la banda de los Van der Linde son personajes memorables, con motivaciones, conflictos y relaciones que te atrapan desde el primer **** realismo y la atención al detalle son impresionantes: cada viaje, cada encuentro y cada tarea secundaria contribuyen a la inmersión. El combate, la caza, la exploración y la interacción con el entorno están tan bien diseñados que incluso las actividades “menores” se sienten **** apartado visual y sonoro es de primer nivel: paisajes que parecen pinturas vivientes, cambios climáticos impactantes y una banda sonora que acompaña perfectamente la tensión o la calma del momento. Todo contribuye a que el juego se sienta cinematográfico sin perder la **** tiene algún pequeño fallo, es que su ritmo pausado y la complejidad de algunas mecánicas pueden no atraer a todos los jugadores, pero para quienes se sumergen en él, cada minuto vale la pena.Conclusión:una experiencia épica, perfecta en narrativa, mundo abierto y detalle; un juego que marca un antes y un después en la industria.Nota final: 10/10

author: Elsendreta3
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2 no es solo un videojuego: es una experiencia completa, viva y brutalmente bien hecha. Su mundo abierto es enorme, detallado y orgánico como pocos en la historia del gaming. Cada ciudad, cada pueblo, cada rincón del mapa se siente como un mundo propio, lleno de vida, personajes memorables y situaciones que te hacen olvidar que estás jugando.
La historia es simplemente puto alucinante. Profunda, madura, emocional y muy humana. Arthur Morgan es uno de los mejores protagonistas jamás creados, y cada decisión, diálogo y relación tiene peso real. No es solo lo que pasa, es cómo te hace sentir. Pocos juegos logran eso.
Gráficamente, es una locura absoluta. Que este juego sea de 2018 es casi insultante para la industria: paisajes impresionantes, animaciones hiperrealistas, iluminación perfecta y un nivel de detalle enfermizo. Todo se mueve, todo respira, todo reacciona a ti.
El sistema de armas, las misiones, los encuentros aleatorios, la interacción con NPCs, la fauna, el clima… todo está muy, muy bien. No hay apartado flojo. Cada personaje es un mundo, cada conversación suma, cada momento importa. Rockstar se pasó el juego.
En resumen: Red Dead Redemption 2 es una obra maestra. Si te gustan los mundos abiertos, las buenas historias o simplemente los videojuegos bien hechos, este juego es obligatorio. Una experiencia que se queda contigo mucho después de pasarte el juego. Para mi un 10, obra maestra en todos los ambitos. Mi unico juego 10 de 10.

author: n1ck-_-sm00th
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is one of those games that reminds you why this medium can be so powerful. The story is absolutely incredible, easily one of the best ever told in a game, and honestly better than many movies I have seen. What really got me was how human everything feels. The characters, the dialogue, the quiet moments, and even the way the world reacts to you all feel natural and believable. Nothing feels rushed or artificial. The game takes its time, and that patience pays off in a big **** world is insanely detailed and alive, but not in a way that screams for attention. It just exists, and you get pulled into it without even realizing how deep you are. I found myself caring about the characters and thinking about the story long after I stopped playing. This is the kind of game you do not want to rush. You want to live in it, explore, listen, and let it unfold at its own pace. If you care about story, atmosphere, and immersion, this is as close to perfect as it gets. For me, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a 10 out of 10 and a game I wish I could experience for the first time all over again.

author: OmniXan
text: At what point does a game transcend mere entertainment and become a true piece of art? I feel confident in saying this is objectively the most immersive and well crafted open world experience available in gaming even 7 years after its release. The amount of detail in the world and freedom to do what you want is unparalleled, you could likely spend hundreds of hours in story mode exploring and doing side content without even playing the main missions aside from the introduction. What's even more impressive is that this game also features what I consider to be the best narrative and cast of characters in any game I've played. I'm not the type to get attached to video game characters, but this cast is so well written that it pleasantly breaks the mold for me and the emotional beats of this story hit me in a way no other game's story has been able to. I will say, however, it does require some patience and appreciation for the experience the developers are trying to convey, realism is often prioritized over convenience, but it's never anything drastic and the trade off is that the world feels real and alive in a way no other games open world does. RDR2 is a title that will always be in the highest echelon of the gaming hall of fame and I think will be looked back on very fondly for many years to come.

author: Wiliiam
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is a life-changing experience. It is the perfect game, as it's very long, so it has mamy stories to tell, the gameplay is just right, it has no changeable difficulty and it's never confusing, never too hard, but never too easy. I believe the best part about this game is the story. It's entertaining and full of plot twists. It's a life changing experience that makes you question the actual meaning of life. That's why you can find videos of people crying after beating the game (myself including). The actors (not voice actors) did a fantastic job, especially Roger Clark, who plays Arthur Morgan. Also, the soundtracks are insane, fitting the scenes excellently (I even ended up listening to them during my everyday life. The have found a way to a play a song at the start/the middle of the game, and during the end play an epic version of it, which makes you nostalgic about a game that you haven't even finished. To sum up, perfect game, Rockstar did a fantastic job on it and it makes it a worthy and even better sequel (technically prequel) to Red Dead Redemption 1.

author: Wiiiliax
text: Que dire, Red dead Redemption 2, Une claque monumentale, que ce soit dans son design et ses graphismes magnifiques qui concurence toujours avec les derniers jeux sorties ces dernières années, son scénario et son histoire digne des plus grands western, et son open world qui regorge d'action et de lieux à explorer. Ce jeu frôle la perfection, son sens du détails presque insolent, ses personnages tellement bien écrit et auquel on s'attache facilement, et les émotions qu'ils nous font traverser. Tout est exeptionnel dans ce jeu. Quand à la lenteur du gamplay, des déplacements d'Arthur ect, je ne le trouve pas du tout gênant, il faut simplement comprendre le jeu, RDR2 et le jeu qui m'a vraiment permis de mieux apprécier jouer, prendre le temps, quitte à passer 20h de plus avant de le terminer, j'ai eu une visions différente sur les jeux vidéo avant et après RDR2, alors pour toute personne qui aurait arrêter au chapitre 1 ou 2 ayant souffert de la lenteur, et bien relancer vous car vous ratez un chef d'oeuvre. Il m'a fallu que je me plonge moi même à plusieurs reprise dans le jeu pour finalement l'apprécier, mais maintenant je l'adore. Et j'espère qu'on aura une touche de RDR2 dans GTA VI.

author: stillergentlman
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 ist für mich das beste Spiel aller Zeiten, weil es nicht versucht, mich permanent zu unterhalten, sondern mir erlaubt, Teil einer Welt zu sein. Alles ist bewusst langsam, schwer und geerdet – vom Reiten über das Schießen bis zu einfachen Alltagsdingen. Genau dadurch entsteht eine Immersion, die kein anderes Spiel **** Spielwelt fühlt sich nicht wie eine Kulisse an, sondern wie ein lebendiger Ort, der auch ohne mich existiert. Begegnungen wirken natürlich, NPCs glaubwürdig, und selbst nach 1.200 Stunden entdeckt man neue Details. Arthur Morgan ist dabei keine Spielfigur, sondern eine der am besten geschriebenen Charaktere überhaupt – seine Entwicklung passiert leise, zwischen den Zeilen, und bleibt lange im Kopf.RDR2 ist perfekt und genau das macht es einzigartig. Es respektiert den Spieler, nimmt sich Zeit und schafft etwas, das kaum ein anderes Spiel schafft: Bedeutung.

author: keymakey
text:
Plot 3/10 — a completely ordinary Western story about nothing. 

Controls 0/10 -- I played on PC. The controls are the most uncomfortable I've ever experienced in any game I've played. The helicopter mission from GTA Vice City on PC in 2003 was more comfortable than all the controls in this game. 

Dynamics 1/10 -- the game has zero dynamics. If you like slow-paced storytelling (and I remind you that the plot is as ordinary as it gets), then you might enjoy it. Quite often, it just gets boring.
Graphics 1/10 -- for this type of game are ordinary, nothing remarkable.

There is no auto-save system -- excuse me, am I playing Dark Souls?

Result: 1/10. Don't understand this game.

author: BuntFugget
text: I wish I had bought a physical copy of Red Dead Redemption 2 so that I could break it. What an expensively polished yet sorry excuse for a game this is. Game is a misnomer, though, more like 300 hours of western references with some light "gameplay" peppered in. What's the most exciting part of a western? The shooting! So how bout make shooting mechanics that don't treat players like they've not only never played a shooter before, but only just learned what a video game was? The delay between every action results in the slowest most boring shootouts since, well, GTA 5. We want you to hunt and be hunted, they promised! Oh, does that mean the animals will attack and evade in challenging and unexpected ways? Haha no it means you spend a fifth of the time hunting and the rest doing hunting related chores! What other mechanics do you ask!? Oh I get to, sorry HAVE TO, make my character bathe and eat and sleep. WOOOAH HOW REALISTIC I get to do the things I'm doing in real life anyway! There's a reason that movies don't show the monotony in between the relevant. Ever seen The Man with No Name bathing or getting dressed? No, because it's BORING! I bet you Rockstar apologists are disappointed they don't have minigames for brushing your teeth or wiping your ass, too. Ooh and let's repeat the same character arc from the last game, and totally waste the title and story that could have been Read Dead Retribution. They should give the license back to Capcom, you know, a company that makes video games, not overproduced monotony simulators.

author: JeansMFJ
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2, sviluppato da Rockstar Games, è il prequel di Red Dead Redemption che ci riporta nell’America del 1899 e ripercorre gli ultimi anni del Far West con una narrazione incredibile.
Trama
La storia segue le vicende di Arthur Morgan e della banda di cui fa parte, comandata da Dutch Van der Linde. In quel periodo l’America stava abbracciando il progresso e con esso le bande di fuorilegge venivano represse rapidamente spingendo quindi la banda a cercare un modo per fuggire sia dal suo passato turbolento sia da questa rapida repressione. Attraverso le missioni della storia principale e quelle secondarie, il gioco ci spingerà a riflettere su questioni etiche e morali e sulle conseguenze delle azioni scelte da ogni **** che incontreremo. 
Gameplay
Red Dead Redemption 2 offre un open world vastissimo, ricco di vita dove, anche durante una lunga cavalcata da un luogo all'altro diventa un’esperienza offrendo anche brevi vicende in cui puoi andare incontro che rendono il tutto più vivo e appagante. Le missioni principali sono più dense e dettagliate, mentre quelle secondarie, sono più brevi ma molto curate ed interessanti. Saranno molto comuni le sparatorie, le esplorazioni e la caccia, mentre il sistema di onore del protagonista ti spinge a prendere delle decisioni in base alla tua morale. La maggior parte del tempo saremo in sella al nostro fidato cavallo, anche se il sistema di movimento non mi ha appagato molto dandomi dei problemi ogni tanto.
Grafica e Audio
Le ambientazioni sono incredibili, anche un breve sentiero o una piccola foresta sono ricche di dettagli, il ciclo giorno/notte e i fenomeni atmosferici contribuiscono ad un’esperienza più appagante. Anche se è uscito nel 2018, la grafica è a livelli altissimi e sembra dei giorni d’oggi. Il doppiaggio in inglese è incredibile, ricco di sfumature e insieme ai suoni ambientali rende tutto quanto più immersivo. Durante i momenti più speciali, come la fine del gioco, ci saranno delle vere e proprie canzoni con testo che sono, a mio parere, fantastiche.
Longevità
Personalmente ho impiegato più di 50 ore per finire la storia principale completando anche gran parte delle missioni secondarie disponibili. Tutti gli eventi casuali e il completismo possono portare la durata di questo gioco a livelli altissimi. Inoltre la modalità multiplayer Red Dead Online, che personalmente non ho ancora giocato, può aumentare la giocabilità di tantissimo.
Conclusione
Penso che Red Dead Redemption II sia uno dei migliori giochi che io abbia mai giocato, è stato complesso per me trovare dei difetti evidenti, come il movimento del cavallo, l’unica cosa che ci tengo a dire è che alcuni potrebbero trovarlo un po’ lento, anche se il gioco offre delle possibilità per velocizzare l’esperienza come il viaggio rapido o la possibilità di saltare le scene. Non ho ancora giocato al primo capitolo, ma essendo un prequel penso non ci siano problemi e che, anzi, possa rendere l’esperienza del capitolo precedente migliore.
Voto = 10

author: DivineFaith
text:
Amazing Open World Game!
Red Dead Redemption 2 is truly a fantastic game. It features an interesting and lively open world, a solid story with a strong prologue and epilogue, still impressive graphics, and absolutely stunning cinematics.
That said, there were a few things that didn’t quite work for me personally. I mean, there were tons of different weapons, but they barely felt different in terms of gameplay. Not to mention the weapon customization, which unfortunately was purely cosmetic and didn’t really affect gameplay. Like the weapon mechanics, the gameplay itself lacked variety. Most missions boiled down to the same basic loop: no money, rob something, lose the money, get hunted, relocate, hunt animals. 
What really bothered me was the control system! It’s clear the game was originally designed for consoles and then ported to PC. I can’t even count how many times I accidentally started a shootout just because I bumped into someone by mistake. 
The game also felt way too drawn out. It would’ve been nice to be able to skip some of the horseback riding, because at times I felt more like I was in a horse simulator than an action-adventure game. The cutscenes were excellent, but that’s kind of the issue — the whole experience often felt more like an interactive movie set in the Wild West, one that wants you to feel the story more than actually play it. 
That aside, you can absolutely tell how much love and care went into this game. The level of detail in the towns and cities is incredible, and a huge amount of time clearly went into the story.
All in all, it’s a really good game that still has some room for improvement, but also does an awful lot right.

author: zwesta
text: Man, after actually finishing Red Dead Redemption 2, I’ve got to say it straight: the game is painfully slow, bloated, and obsessed with its own ‘cinematic’ ego. Yeah, the world looks gorgeous, but when every damn action takes five seconds and half the missions feel like chores, immersion turns into pure frustration. Arthur’s story deserved better pacing, not this dragged-out marathon that constantly kills the momentum. It’s a masterpiece stuck inside a swamp of pointless animations and overhyped storytelling—and playing it often felt more like a tedious job than an adventure.

author: Ali_Akdemir
text: 75 saatin sonunda bu başyapıtı bitirmiş durumdayım. Oyunda ana görev, bütün yan görevler, ödül avcısı ve birkaç efsanevi hayvan görevi yaptım. Oyun hakkındaki görüşlerim şu şekilde Grafik konusunda bu oyundan daha iyi bir yapım olduğunu görmedim. Animasyonlar mükemmel ve animasyon yapısı olarak bu oyunun kalitesinde birkaç tane daha oyun var. Oyunun başı yavaş açılıyor yorumlarına da şöyle bir örnek ile açıklayabilirim. Çok iyi bir film ilk 10-15 dakikasında izleyiciyi kendine çekemeyebilir veya etkilemeyebilir veya çok iyi bir dizi ilk bölümlerinde bunu yapamayabilir. Bu oyunda da o mevzu söz konusu bence. Zaten oyunda 6 bölüm ve 2 ek bölüm var. Oyun bana kalırsa 2. bölüme geçtiğin an ve seni dünyada açık bir şekilde gezmeye bıraktığı an, oyun nasıl bir şaheser oluğunu sana gösteriyor ve oyuncuyu içine çekmeyi başarıyor. Oyunda karakter gelişimi mükemmel seviyede ve çok iyi akılda kalıcı ve yaratıcı karakterlere sahip. Oyunun ortalarına doğru önemli bir olay oluyor ve bu olaydan sonra oyunun sonuna kadar oyun mükemmellik konusunda top seviyeye çıkıyor. Oyunun sonunda kontrol John'a geçtikten sonra John ile oynama isteğim gelmedi ve direkt farklı bir karakter ile oynadığımı hissettim.  Oyunun müzikleri gayet iyi yaklaşık 5 tane mükemmel soundtrack var ve bazı soundtracklerin girdiği yerlerde insanı feci vuruyor. Oyunda tek sıkıntı bulduğum nokta John'un çiftliğini kurması için yaptığımız görev şeması biraz sıktı. Onun dışında oyun tamamen bir şaheser ve kesinlikle indirimde 15 doları hak eden mükemmel bir yapım.

author: LUXOID
text: For me, Red Dead Redemption 2 is simply a perfect game. It’s more than a video game—it’s an experience, it’s life. From the very beginning, you enter a world that feels truly alive and believable. Every detail, every interaction, every person you meet makes it feel like you’re really living in the old West. It’s like being transported to another time. Technically, it’s incredible even today. Sometimes the horse would bug out a bit, but when you look at the overall beauty and complexity of the world, it’s something you can easily forgive. The story is beautiful and makes you fall in love with the good characters and genuinely hate the bad ones. When characters you’ve grown attached to die, you really feel it—at least that’s how it was for me. The side missions are amazing and add a lot to the main experience, especially the one with the nun that actually changes a main story cutscene. Arthur Morgan is written perfectly. I loved him, I rooted for him, and I genuinely cared about him—a feeling I’ve rarely had for any other video game character. The original voice acting is fantastic, with accents and performances that make the world feel even more authentic and immersive. It’s a game that should be enjoyed slowly, taking in every moment and every detail. Personally, I even prefer it to the GTA series. GTA games are fun but more goofy, while Red Dead Redemption 2 feels like a mature, emotional work of art. In short, it’s a masterpiece—an unforgettable experience that sets a new standard for storytelling in gaming.

author: sagaschalant
text:
mano, eu nem sei por onde começar direito porque red dead redemption 2 é aquele tipo de jogo que não dá pra explicar totalmente pra quem nunca jogou, só quem viveu entende, tá ligado? é um bagulho que vai muito além de só atirar, cavalgar e fazer missão, é literalmente uma experiência, uma jornada, um filme interativo que te puxa pra dentro do mundo dele de um jeito absurdo

desde o começo, quando o jogo te joga naquela nevasca no prólogo, tu já sente o peso da história, o clima pesado, a sensação de que tudo aquilo é real, o frio, o som dos cavalos pisando na neve, a respiração dos personagens, tudo tem um nível de detalhe que tu não vê em nenhum outro jogo. parece que cada pedacinho do mapa foi feito à mão, com um cuidado surreal

os personagens são outro nível. o arthur morgan é, pra mim, o melhor protagonista já feito em um jogo. ele não é aquele herói perfeito, ele é humano, tem falhas, tem arrependimentos, mas também tem um coração gigante. o jeito que ele muda ao longo da história é muito real. tu começa achando que ele é só mais um fora da lei, e termina o jogo chorando por ele, entendendo tudo que ele passou, tudo que ele sentiu. é impossível não se apegar

e o resto da gangue também é incrível. cada um tem sua personalidade, seus momentos, suas histórias. o dutch é um personagem que tu começa admirando e termina odiando, e isso mostra o quão bem escrito ele é. o john, o sadie, o charles, o javier, até os secundários têm carisma. parece que tu realmente vive com eles, como se fosse parte da gangue mesmo

a história é simplesmente perfeita. não tem pressa, é contada no ritmo certo. tem momentos calmos, de pura contemplação, e outros intensos, que te deixam sem fôlego. e o melhor é que o jogo te recompensa por aproveitar devagar, por explorar, por conversar com as pessoas, por pescar, caçar, tocar violão perto da fogueira, por viver ali

o mundo é o mais vivo que eu já vi num jogo. tu pode só andar de cavalo e sempre vai acontecer alguma coisa — um assalto, um cara pedindo ajuda, um estranho com uma história aleatória. e tudo isso parece natural, nada forçado. tu sente que tá num mundo real, onde tudo continua acontecendo mesmo se tu não estiver olhando

os gráficos nem tem o que falar, né? é absurdo. o pôr do sol batendo nas montanhas, a chuva molhando o casaco, o barulho do rio, o som do vento nas árvores, é tudo tão lindo que às vezes eu só parava e ficava olhando. e mesmo anos depois do lançamento, ainda é um dos jogos mais bonitos já feitos

a trilha sonora é outro ponto que me pegou demais. cada música combina perfeitamente com o momento. tem hora que toca uma canção triste e tu só fica parado, refletindo, e parece que o jogo sabe o que tu tá sentindo. o tema do arthur é simplesmente inesquecível

o final... cara, o final me destruiu. eu nunca chorei com jogo, mas com esse não teve como. é um encerramento perfeito pra uma história perfeita. é aquele tipo de coisa que te deixa um vazio depois, tipo “e agora?”. depois que termina, tu sente falta daquele mundo, daqueles personagens. eu fiquei dias pensando nisso, sem vontade de jogar mais nada

o red dead redemption 2 é o tipo de jogo que mostra o que os videogames podem ser de verdade. é arte, é emoção, é narrativa, é gameplay, é tudo junto. é uma experiência completa que te marca pra sempre

até hoje, nenhum jogo chegou nem perto do que ele me fez sentir. dá pra ver que a rockstar colocou alma em cada detalhe. tu sente isso em cada missão, cada conversa, cada pôr do sol

é um jogo que te faz desacelerar, prestar atenção nas pequenas coisas, sentir o peso das escolhas, e isso é raro. ele não é sobre ganhar, é sobre viver

pra mim, é o melhor jogo de todos os tempos, e eu falo isso sem medo de parecer exagerado. ele é mais do que só um jogo — é uma lembrança que eu vou levar pra sempre.

author: LootArchiv
text:
The pacing of this game was just phenomenal. I know a lot of people complain about a "slow start" or a "slow pace" in general, but that truly is the beauty of this title. You truly appreciate walking in a town, in camp, in stores and so on. This game makes you breathe in the whole experience and doesn`t just rush right through the story and its general world. It really makes you appreciate the small details like dialogues of NPCs, wildlife, the animations of the characters etc. Truly refreshing even tho the story is about 40+ hours long. I just wanted to keep it going the more i came to the end of it. Even after finishing the main game i just kept exploring, looking at things and appreciating the world building mixed with the atmosphere of lightning, NPCs and audio. Of course the characters in this game are written beautifully showing the best and worst of mankind.

Must play.

10/10

author: johko
text:
This is not a great game. Maybe it was overhyped for me. Maybe I just can’t get into AAA games. It has all of the pitfalls of a big name game: clumsy walking, way too many “collectibles” and achievements, NPCs yelling “What’s your problem?!” when you walk past them, accidentally hitting the wrong button and starting a civil war. That kind of thing.

But let’s get to the specifics of what makes this game bad. Red Dead Redemption 2 is a glorified horseback riding simulator. You see how many hours I have on this game? Half of those hours were spent on my phone playing Pokémon TCG while I waited for my character, Arthur, to get to his destination while making very uninteresting conversation with some very uninteresting characters. Every so often they float an option to choose a conversation topic and ask about one thing or another, which is about as interesting and meaningful as the aforementioned conversations. And this doesn’t even count the travel I had to do to get to the mission in the first place. Thank goodness Rockstar was self-aware enough to add a cinematic mode that takes the reins so I could at least play some Pokémon while I wait.

What went wrong? What made Half-life 2 so revolutionary was that the story was happening all around you while you were still playing the game. There are no cut scenes and they never take control from you, unless they are literally strapping you down for a lab procedure. Now, I’m not saying that every game should be like this, but Red Dead Redemption 2 takes a half-measure approach that fails miserably. It’s like they liked the idea of giving the player the freedom to do what they want but they realized that it clashed with their other objectives. You’ll approach a mission zone and Arthur will automatically dismount and start walking. You can’t run in the base camp. I guess it’s rude or something. Sometimes your horse will even be completely controlled by the game and you won’t know it unless you try to move in another direction. It’s just not always clear what the rules are and being teased with freedom to have it be continually yanked away is frustrating.

The game does have its merits though. The environment is incredibly rich and the spirit of historical accuracy is astonishing. This game made me genuinely interested in outlaw life during this time period. I also really enjoyed hunting (almost as much as I enjoyed lassoing and hogtying NPCs). And there are loads of really cool customization options for your outfit and your horse. One of my favorite details is the fact that your facial hair will grow and you have the ability to shave it the way you want. The characters are incredibly well-acted as well. It’s a shame that the quality acting doesn’t have a story to match.

Moral choices are always an interesting mechanic to me. The struggle to do good when you have so much to lose is at the heart of the human experience. Clearly, this is an overarching theme in RDR2, with the good boy/bad boy meter. But this theme is executed with another half-measure approach. Throughout the game, Arthur is given the option of donating money to the Church, or letting a man live, or helping a damsel in distress. These are not exactly difficult moral decisions to make. But that’s not the problem I have. The problem is that while you make these choices, the game requires you to kill, beat, and rob others senselessly to make progress. And then Arthur portrays himself as some kind of misunderstood antihero. And I just don’t believe him.

If you treat this game for what it is, a glorified horseback riding sim, it’s the best one out there.

Verdict: BAD

author: Cat_Me
text: O "Red Dead Redemption 2" é uma obra-prima que redefine o conceito de beleza nos jogos eletrônicos. Desenvolvido pela Rockstar Games, esse jogo não é apenas uma experiência de jogo; é uma jornada imersiva que transporta você para o Velho Oeste americano no final do século XIX. Vamos mergulhar nos detalhes que tornam esse jogo tão incrivelmente lindo e envolvente.O Mundo Aberto: Um Quadro VivoO mundo de "Red Dead Redemption 2" é vasto e meticulosamente detalhado. Desde as vastidões das pradarias até as montanhas nevadas e os pântanos sombrios, cada ambiente foi criado com uma atenção impressionante aos detalhes. A iluminação, as condições climáticas e as mudanças de estação não são apenas visuais; elas afetam a jogabilidade e a interação com o mundo ao seu redor. A sensação de explorar esse mundo é indescritível – cada esquina pode revelar um segredo, um encontro inesperado ou uma vista de tirar o fôlego.Gráficos e Animação: Realismo ImpressionanteOs gráficos do "Red Dead Redemption 2" são impressionantes, com uma fidelidade visual que rivaliza com filmes de Hollywood. As texturas, as luzes e as sombras são tão realistas que você pode se perder na beleza do mundo. As animações dos personagens são igualmente impressionantes, com movimentos naturais e expressões faciais que capturam as emoções de Arthur Morgan e dos outros personagens com uma profundidade surpreendente.Trilha Sonora: Um Acréscimo EmocionalA trilha sonora do jogo, composta por músicas country, folk e clássicas, complementa perfeitamente a atmosfera do Velho Oeste. Cada faixa foi escolhida para evocar emoções específicas, desde a melancolia das paisagens desoladas até a adrenalina dos tiroteios. A música não é apenas um pano de fundo; ela é uma parte integral da experiência, guiando suas emoções e imergindo você ainda mais no mundo de Arthur Morgan.História e Personagens: Profundidade e ComplexidadeA história de "Red Dead Redemption 2" é uma das mais bem escritas e emocionais dos últimos anos. Seguindo a vida de Arthur Morgan, um membro da gangue Van der Linde, o jogo explora temas de lealdade, redenção e a luta pela sobrevivência em um mundo que está mudando rapidamente. Os personagens são complexos e multifacetados, com histórias de fundo que os tornam reais e relacionáveis. Cada escolha que você faz tem consequências, não apenas na história principal, mas também nas interações com os outros personagens.Jogabilidade: Uma Experiência RicaA jogabilidade de "Red Dead Redemption 2" é incrivelmente rica e variada. Desde a caça e a pesca até os tiroteios e as missões, cada atividade foi projetada para ser envolvente e satisfatória. O sistema de tiro é responsivo e desafiador, e as mecânicas de furtividade e estratégia adicionam uma camada extra de profundidade. E, claro, a interação com o mundo – alimentar cavalos, conversar com NPCs, explorar – tudo contribui para uma experiência de jogo imersiva.Conclusão: Uma Obra-Prima do Gênero"Red Dead Redemption 2" não é apenas um jogo; é uma experiência de arte. É uma obra-prima que combina narrativa emocional, jogabilidade envolvente e uma beleza visual impressionante. Se você ainda não jogou, prepare-se para uma jornada que vai tocar seu coração e expandir seus horizontes. E se você já jogou, sabe do que estou falando – é uma experiência inesquecível que permanece com você muito depois de terminar o jogo.

author: DarkFox22
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 remains, even in 2025, one of the greatest masterpieces in the video game industry, offering a unique experience which elevates open world games, with an immersive narrative and an incredibly detailed **** most noticeable aspect of this title is without a doubt its ridiculous level of detail, which makes players forget they’re in a video game and instead feel like they’re under an outlaw's skin in the Wild West. NPCs have daily routines, remember past interactions, and may even confront the player later on based on previous choices. Animals behave realistically — hunting, fighting, scratching against trees, or even mourning the death of their pack **** game is also filled with small touches: corpses decomposing over time, realistic eating animations, or the genuine sense of loss when your horse dies. These are just a few examples; I could have written a second bible dedicated solely to the game’s **** story of Arthur Morgan (the protagonist) is not only captivating but also emotionally complex, allowing players to create a deep bound with him.  They nailed it with the writing and the voice actor cast, which made the characters gain life and authenticity. Rockstar managed the impossible, making almost every character memorable, whether through their charisma, ambitions, or personal struggles. This also creates the perfect bridge to play the previous title in the franchise, which is actually the sequel, since it continues the story and makes the ending of Red Dead Redemption 1 even more impactful for those who played this game first.Rockstar once again adopted its classic game design formula for linear open-world missions that take you from point A to point B with clear instructions on the interface. However, this time, player choice plays a more significant role, since it affects not only the storyline but also how people react to Arthur, which adds an extra layer of depth to the **** core mechanics of the franchise return (combat both gunplay and melee, horseback riding, crafting, item purchasing), but all of them have been improved, with special emphasis on combat and the honor system. Combat feels more refined, with a wider variety of weapons and distinct mechanics.  However, you can’t carry them all at once, like in the previous game you’re forced to store some in your chest or on your horse and can only carry a few weapons, which can be a little frustrating when you are faced with unexpected combat encounters. The honor system also gained greater importance, influencing not just rewards but also social **** mechanics, such as fishing, were added, while others, like property ownership, were left out a missed opportunity, especially considering how richly detailed the game’s interiors **** course, this game has its flaws. It has an online mode which sounds exciting at first, but it quickly becomes repetitive and boring due to a lack of content. Another problem is that after finishing the story, players can still explore the world of Red Dead, but there isn’t much left to do apart from clearing unfinished side missions and hunting collectibles for 100% completion. It would have been great to have repayable bounty hunter missions like in the previous **** sum up, Red Dead Redemption 2 remains, to this day, the king of open-world games. Despite its flaws, its profound story and obsessive attention to detail make it a must-play for all gamers.

author: DG16
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2 – Review

An in-depth journey through Old America You will never forget!

Red Dead Redemption 2 from the beloved Rockstar had so many positive reviews, I had to play it. And I have to say after playing, this is why Rockstar is the best! The game has such a good story with twists and heist to tie in everything. It features some of the best graphics and physics I have ever seen in a game (Even compared to modern games of today). And that’s not it!The game has so much to explore, so many animals, even though it’s not a Far Cry game, and it features great action mechanics which I was expecting since they are an upgrade of GTA 5. Honestly I have so much to explain but I can’t do it without spoiling the game, It just is in my top 5 best video games of all time, maybe even top 3. Just play it and have a great time as Arthur Morgan!

PROS:
-	The Game has everything you will ever need.
-	The story has many angles and side missions are in a league of their own.
-	The mechanics and graphics are breathtaking.
-	Truly a game of the decade.

CONS:
-	We are in a time where games need strong hardware and unfortunately this is no exception. But even on Low settings, It doesn’t disappoint.

RATING: 10/10

author: sarecW
text:
Unfortunately, games like this are holding the industry back. Rockstar is a stupid company that doesn't know how to make games. The story is a cliché mafia story, but more importantly, it's full of filler and the plot repeats itself. The pacing and storytelling are garbage. The exaggerated drama is ridiculous. The main and supporting characters are garbage. They are cliché characters based on familiar stereotypes. Arthur Morgan is a whiny moron. He's inconsistent, passive, and weak. Most importantly, he's aimless compared to John Marston. He's a dumb, average outlaw with no brains. He has no problem killing anyone, but when it comes to Dutch, he suddenly becomes a moralist. Dutch abandons him to die, but Arthur the moron keeps doing whatever Dutch tells him to do. Of course, he never stops whining. He's a shallow, artificial, characterless "character." Random encounters and stranger missions are overly scripted and boring fetch quests. There's no creativity. Most of the time, they're based on helping someone who's gotten into trouble. The praise for these is ridiculous. They were already in the first game, and they were better executed there. In this game, NPC interaction is extremely limited. You're doing the same things over and over, and it gets boring after a while. There's no freedom or variety in the main quests. You're constantly robbing places, fighting, and taking down 20 guys in every mission. ("The heist didn't go as planned" theme) Too much action undermines realism and immersion. Side quests are just tedious fetch quests. Gunplay is bad, so hunting and such are uninteresting. The animations are nice, though. The map is too generic and doesn't feel handcrafted. It feels empty. Everywhere looks the same except for the snowy areas. The biomes lack **** controls are a complete mess. They're overly clunky and ruin the gameplay and fun. The game can't even be called open world due to the scripted gameplay and limited interaction. Casual players who call this the best open world probably only play 1-2 video games a year. The graphics praise is exaggerated and ridiculous. There are tons of games released in 2018 and earlier that look better. The textures are blurry in some places. There are TAA issues.

Aren't you tired of playing the same nonsense since GTA 4, fanboys? Even COD, which comes out every year, is much more innovative and experimental compared to Rockstar, which releases a game every 5-6 years. It's the same as Red Dead Revolver, a cheap western where you kill millions of people with an obsession for being like a movie.

Having played and loved the first game prior to playing RDR2, this game just blew me away. It has its flaws, can be a bit clunky (nowhere near as bad as the first game), it can leave you frustrated at times. But man is it a masterpiece. So many times I would boot up the game, play for a few hours and realise I haven't completed a single mission in that duration. Because the exploration and the detail of the world is so easy to get lost in.

The story is somewhat limited in its nature due to being a prequel. I hope for something fully original next from Rockstar.

author: Leo_XO21
text: "Red Dead Redemption 2" stands as one of the greatest achievements in gaming history. Far ahead of its time, its visuals remain astonishing even years after release. Beyond its technical mastery, the game delivers a profound narrative — a beautifully constructed prequel to its predecessor. What begins as an action-driven odyssey unfolds into an emotional journey centered on Arthur Morgan, the loyal companion of John Marston, the first game’s protagonist. The richness of the dialogue and the depth of its lore breathe life into the world; even the smallest conversations feel meticulously crafted, elevating the immersion to an unparalleled level. One of the most compelling aspects lies in the ambiguity of certain characters’ fates. By leaving their futures to speculation, the story extends beyond the screen, allowing the player’s imagination to keep the world alive. Finally, its ambitious and surprisingly expansive epilogue bridges the gap to the original Red Dead Redemption seamlessly. Together, both titles form a narrative duology of rare depth and artistry — an essential experience for anyone who considers video games a medium of storytelling as much as entertainment.

author: UtkuGorgun
text: Rockstar Games’in 2018 tarihli başyapıtı Red Dead Redemption 2, yalnızca bir oyun değil; yaşayan, soluyan ve oyuncusuyla derin bağlar kurabilen bir dijital roman. 188 saatin ardından dahi oyuncusunu içine çekmeye devam eden, bitmesin istenen bir yolculuk… Red Dead Redemption 2’yi benzersiz kılan en temel unsurlardan biri, oyuncuya sıradan bir açık dünya deneyimi sunmak yerine, ona bu dünyanın gerçek bir parçası olma hissini yaşatmasıdır. Oyunun nefes kesici doğa manzaraları, dinamik hava koşulları ve detaylara gösterilen titizlik, oyuncuya adeta fiziksel bir varlık hissi verir. Kırlarda at sürmenin, dağlık yollarda ilerlemenin ya da şehir merkezinde insanların arasına karışmanın her biri, meditatif ve neredeyse şiirsel bir deneyime dönüşür. Ancak bu başyapıtı asıl unutulmaz kılan unsur, tartışmasız bir şekilde Arthur Morgan karakteridir. Morgan yalnızca bir ana karakter değil, oyuncunun duygusal bir yansıması, vicdani bir pusulası ve nihayetinde bir dostudur. Hikâye boyunca yaşanan olaylar, Arthur’un içsel dönüşümüyle birleşerek, karakter gelişimi anlamında video oyun tarihinde nadir görülen bir derinliğe ulaşır. Oyunun antagonistleri Micah ve Dutch ise nefret duygusunu öylesine ustalıkla tetikler ki, oyuncu ile karakter arasındaki bağ, sadece sempati üzerinden değil; adalet duygusu üzerinden de pekişir. Bu da Rockstar’ın yazarlık konusunda ulaştığı yüksek seviyeyi açıkça gösterir. Red Dead Redemption 2, oyuncunun yalnızca vakit geçirdiği bir eğlence ürünü değil; onunla birlikte düşündüğü, hissettiği ve sonunda ayrılmakta zorlandığı bir yaşam kesiti sunar. Bitmesini istemeyeceğiniz bir hikâye, terk etmek istemeyeceğiniz bir dünya ve unutamayacağınız bir yol arkadaşlığıdır.

author: kaydist
text:
RDR2 not only has one of the best stories in entertainment history, it did so with class and respect to historical events of 1800's America and prior due to the implications of the past for example the Wapiti Native Americans.. their story begins at their end they've fought long enough to be exhausted of all hope.. perhaps they aren't the only ones.

Arthur Morgan, I will speak from his positive honor self because that's who I know him as.. he's such a humble soul, he came from nothing with no one to support him and that made him fight hard all his life, he carries everyone on his back and expected only decency.. honor in return. as much as I've stated before that you can't be a good guy when you do the acts the Van Der Linde Gang does against his best wishes or not you can only be an anti-hero and I believe Arthur is the perfect anti-hero who's wraith is very rarely used for malice. this is a spoiler-less review so I'll just say the things this man has to endure shows the limit of what one can endure, and it's never about him. Mr. Morgan is by far my favorite protagonist ever written.

the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 is simply gorgeous, to me it is still unmatched in ambition 7 years after release.. games have matched it in texture quality, lighting quality and in some ways mechanics quality but never in the open world setting.. RDR2 is the diamond standard of an Open World title.. I would expect nothing less from the ever genre defining studio Rockstar Games. the world evolves throughout the game like the Appleseed Timber site in West Elizabeth near Strawberry that will be completely deforested throughout the story, new train tracks are being built and you get to see the completion of them, the town of Valentine has a building being constructed that finishes construction towards the end of the main story and same with a property just south of Valentine.

RDR2 also has an excellent modding community, this is kind of a trait that all Rockstar titles will share but never the less it does. I especially love all the horse texture mods the community makes and new clothing/hairstylers for Arthur. 

I've put a total of 700 hours into Red Dead 2, I've gotten 98% competition.. I know this game inside and out and I can tell you confidently it's incredible.  10/10.

author: Cybernaut
text:
A Symphony of Six-Shooters and Sunsets -- 10/10

Rockstar did not just make any game. They carved an epic into the digital stone.

RDR2 is a cinematic, slow-burning masterpiece that rides tall on every front. The story is a heartfelt outlaw opera, rich with tension, tenderness, and tobacco-chewing charm. Arthur Morgan isn’t just a protagonist, he’s a philosophy in motion, delivered through unforgettable missions that range from shootouts to quiet, haunting moments under open skies.

Visually, it’s jaw-dropping. The world breathes, trees sway, mud squelches, and sunsets bleed gold. Every gunshot snaps like a whip, from the pull of the level action to the click of the revolver--and the soundtrack? A moody, melancholic marvel that lingers long after the credits. Add in lifelike NPCs, dynamic wildlife, and an atmosphere thicker than Saint-Denis fog—it’s no wonder this game stole hearts (and hundreds of hours).

Cons: None worth chasing on horseback.

Verdict: Get it and let this legend bury itself in your heart.

Multiplayer not included in this review, to keep it as honest as Arthur’s best intentions.
