author: Faelzera
text:
Faltam palavras para definir esse jogo, uma das, senão a melhor obra áudio-visual que já tive o prazer de jogar, me divertir, emocionar e se arrepiar a cada momento. Toda vez que abro esse jogo fico bobo e estonteado com sua beleza e seu mundo vivo, que beiram a perfeição, mostrando que Ray tracing não é pre requisito para criar um ambiente realista e imersivo. Esse não somente é o Jogo do ano, em seu lançamento, como o melhor de sua geração e, o melhor de todos os tempos. para mim. Independente de seu gênero e gosto pessoal, por exemplo, meu jogo preferido é o Dark Souls, o primeiro, foi nele que comecei a enxergar jogos de vídeo-game, como obras de arte, foi meu divisor de águas. Mas voltando ao Red Dead 2. A trilha sonora, a ambientação, tudo, é um absurdo. E o que dizer do Arthur Morgan, que para quem jogou essa obra-prima, acho quase impossível ele não se tornar seu personagem preferido ou estar entre os melhores. Mesmo com tudo isso, esse jogo não foi um dos mais premiados da história, o que só prova o quanto esses prêmios e essa ´´Crítica Especializada´´, assim como no meio artístico do cinema, são totalmente parciais e tendenciosos. Deixo aqui minha carta de Amor para esse jogo, simplesmente sou grato á Deus por ter tido a oportunidade de vivenciar essa história em 2 momentos diferentes de minha vida e também, obrigado RockStar, por nos presentar com essa Pintura. Só um adendo, o Online infelizmente é totalmente deixado de lado, desde o lançamento quando joguei no xbox one, era horrível, agora em 2023, no Pc, continua cheio de problemas e vários Bugs, infelizmente. 
Apesar desse ponto negativo do modo Online é ´´A´´ Obra Prima Absoluta!

text: Red Dead Redemption 2 sur PC est, à mes yeux, une véritable œuvre d’art vidéoludique. Rockstar a repoussé les limites du genre open world en livrant une expérience d’une richesse, d’un réalisme et d’une profondeur rarement atteints. La version PC sublime le jeu avec une finesse graphique incroyable, une fluidité bien supérieure aux consoles (à condition d’avoir une bonne configuration), et de nombreuses options techniques pour personnaliser **** qui m’a marqué avant tout, c’est l’immersion. Le monde de RDR2 est vivant, crédible, et réagit de manière organique à nos actions. Les détails sont partout : dans les dialogues, les animations, les comportements des PNJ, les changements météorologiques, ou encore la gestion du cheval et de l’équipement. On sent que chaque élément a été pensé avec **** scénario est puissant, émouvant et superbement interprété. Arthur Morgan est un des meilleurs personnages jamais écrits dans un jeu vidéo, avec une évolution complexe et humaine. Le rythme du jeu peut paraître lent pour certains, mais il sert parfaitement l’ambiance western et la narration.Musique, gameplay, direction artistique, écriture, performance technique : tout frôle la perfection. Bien sûr, aucun jeu n’est parfait pour tout le monde, mais Red Dead Redemption 2 m’a offert une expérience inoubliable, qui dépasse largement le cadre du simple divertissement.

author: Lennon-S
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is one of those rare, transformative works. It’s more than just a video game. It is, in the truest sense of the word, a modern epic—one that demands to be discussed alongside the greatest achievements in cinematic storytelling, literature, and interactive design.This is a game that succeeds on virtually every front. The writing is some of the finest ever committed to pixels. Arthur Morgan—complex, principled, flawed, introspective—is not just one of gaming’s greatest protagonists; he’s a fully realized character who could comfortably sit beside cinema’s best antiheroes. His journey is devastating and beautiful, a meditation on loyalty, redemption, decay, and the passage of time. Rockstar didn’t just create a compelling story—they crafted a narrative experience that unfolds with all the subtlety, gravity, and nuance **** American **** then there’s the world itself. This isn’t just an open world—it’s a living, breathing historical simulation. Every detail, every shadow, every gust of wind through the trees of the Heartlands feels meticulously placed. The architecture, the wildlife, the NPC behavior, the dynamic weather—it all exists not merely to entertain, but to immerse. It’s a world that invites introspection and rewards the patient player. There’s a stillness, a rhythm, that mirrors life itself—something games almost never attempt, let alone **** course, not everyone sees it. In fact, many of the loudest criticisms you’ll find online come not from professional critics or thoughtful players, but from a particular demographic of younger, attention-deficient reviewers. These are the same voices lamenting the absence of cars in a Western, or complaining about having to brush their horse as if basic immersion were somehow an inconvenience. They mistake contemplative pacing for boredom, and character-driven narrative for tedium. Their grievances reveal far more about their own shallow expectations than about the game itself.This isn’t surprising. We live in an era where reactionary culture often overrides thoughtful critique. Nuance is replaced with knee-jerk opinions, and intellectual patience is dismissed as pretentious. There is a generation of players so conditioned by instant gratification and dopamine-fueled game loops that the deliberate, meaningful storytelling of Red Dead Redemption 2 feels alien to them. They want GTA in a cowboy hat—and when they don’t get it, they lash out with all the critical depth of a Reddit meme **** Red Dead Redemption 2 wasn’t made for them. It was made for those who can appreciate a story told with care and intention. For those who understand that emotional payoff is earned, not handed out. For those who value character development, moral ambiguity, and an unflinching look at the myths and realities of the American ****’s amusing, in a way, how many of these critics decry Hollywood’s lack of originality while simultaneously rejecting a game like this—one of the most ambitious and original storytelling efforts in the history of the medium—simply because it doesn’t fit neatly into their fast-food consumption model of entertainment. That contradiction alone reveals the fragility of their ****’s be clear: if Red Dead Redemption 2 had been a film, it would have swept the Academy Awards. Best Picture. Best Director. Best Actor. Best Score. Best Screenplay. Its cinematic gravitas is so undeniable that comparisons to The Assassination of Jesse James or There Will Be Blood feel not only fair but necessary. And yet, it is in this very medium—interactive entertainment—that it shines brightest, because it allows the player to live the story, not just witness **** a world increasingly filled with content designed to be devoured and forgotten, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a reminder that some experiences are meant to be absorbed slowly, pondered deeply, and remembered forever. It is a masterpiece—towering, uncompromising, and profoundly **** dismiss it with hollow complaints or adolescent grievances is not just to miss the point—it is to willingly blind oneself to what might very well be one of the greatest accomplishments in modern storytelling. And if that sounds dramatic, it’s only because Red Dead Redemption 2 truly is that extraordinary.

author: Revoo
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is a masterpiece that redefines what it means to be an open-world game. Its world-building, storytelling, and immersive mechanics are second to none. The level of detail in every aspect of the game—whether it's the landscape, NPC interactions, or even the smallest object—is unmatched in the industry. While the slow pacing, occasional repetitiveness, and control issues can be drawbacks, they are minor compared to the sheer quality of the experience. The game remains a landmark achievement in gaming, one that will stand the test of time. Its legacy is undeniable, influencing modern game design and setting new standards for realism. Few games can match its depth, making it one of the most celebrated titles in gaming history. If you haven’t played it yet, there’s no better time to experience one of the best video games ever made. Red Dead Redemption 2 is an absolute must-play.

author: NelsonAlejandro
text: Rockstar Games has long been synonymous with delivering groundbreaking, immersive experiences, but Red Dead Redemption 2 (RDR2) transcends even their lofty standards. Released in 2018, this epic tale of the Wild West has redefined what players can expect from open-world games. Its meticulous attention to detail, emotionally gripping story, and unparalleled gameplay mechanics make it deserving of a perfect 10/10 rating on Metacritic.A Story That Stirs the SoulAt its heart, RDR2 is a character-driven narrative that chronicles the journey of Arthur Morgan, an outlaw struggling with loyalty, morality, and survival. Set against the backdrop of a dying Wild West, the story captures the inevitable clash between freedom and modernization. The narrative is a rollercoaster of emotions, drawing players deep into the lives of the Van der Linde gang. Each character, from the enigmatic Dutch Van der Linde to the tragic John Marston, feels fully realized, with their own motivations, struggles, and arcs. Rarely does a game so seamlessly blend cinematic storytelling with player **** Immersive Open WorldThe open world of RDR2 is nothing short of a marvel. Every corner of the map, from the snowy peaks of Ambarino to the swamps of Lemoyne, bursts with life and realism. Wildlife roams freely, NPCs follow their own routines, and random events add an element of unpredictability. Whether you’re hunting legendary animals, fishing in serene lakes, or encountering a stranger in need, the world feels organic and alive.This level of detail isn’t just aesthetic; it’s functional. For instance, weather changes impact gameplay—rain makes roads muddy, slowing your horse, while snow affects visibility and stamina. Rockstar’s dedication to realism immerses players in a way few games ever achieve.Gameplay: A Blend of Realism and FunRDR2’s gameplay is a masterclass in balancing realism with enjoyment. The gunplay feels weighty and satisfying, whether you’re in a tense standoff or a chaotic shootout. The Dead Eye system, which lets players slow time to line up perfect shots, is as thrilling as **** game’s robust mechanics extend beyond combat. The camp system encourages interaction with gang members, fostering a sense of community. Horse bonding mechanics make your steed an integral part of your journey, while detailed customization options for weapons, outfits, and even your facial hair allow for a deeply personal experience.Unprecedented Attention to DetailWhat truly sets RDR2 apart is its obsessive attention to detail. Rockstar didn’t just create a world; they brought it to life with an astonishing level of realism. NPCs remember your actions, animals decay realistically over time, and even Arthur’s health changes depending on his diet and activity level. The game rewards exploration with countless hidden secrets, from treasure hunts to eerie supernatural encounters.Visual and Audio ExcellenceVisually, RDR2 is breathtaking. Its lush landscapes, dynamic lighting, and realistic animations make every scene a work of art. Combined with a hauntingly beautiful score by Woody Jackson, the game’s atmosphere is nothing short of mesmerizing. The voice acting is equally stellar, with Roger Clark’s performance as Arthur Morgan being a standout. His portrayal of a man torn between loyalty and redemption is nothing less than award-worthy.Themes and DepthBeyond its gameplay and visuals, RDR2 explores profound themes—loyalty, freedom, morality, and the cost of progress. It’s a game that encourages introspection, making players question their own choices and the nature of humanity. Few games dare to tackle such weighty subjects, and even fewer succeed as brilliantly as **** It Deserves 10/10 on MetacriticRDR2 isn’t just a game; it’s an experience that stays with you long after the credits roll. It pushes the boundaries of storytelling, world-building, and gameplay, setting a new standard for the industry. Its flaws, while present, are minor and do little to detract from the overall brilliance of the **** a medium often criticized for prioritizing profits over creativity, Red Dead Redemption 2 stands as a testament to what happens when a developer pours their heart and soul into a project. It’s a game that not only deserves a perfect score on Metacritic but also a place in the pantheon of all-time greats.ConclusionRed Dead Redemption 2 is more than a game; it’s a masterpiece that encapsulates the very essence of what makes gaming a unique and powerful art form. Its unmatched attention to detail, emotional depth, and breathtaking world make it a must-play for anyone who appreciates storytelling, immersion, or simply great gameplay. Rockstar Games has delivered a timeless classic, and giving it anything less than a perfect 10/10 would be an injustice to the sheer brilliance of its design.

author: seriousboris
text: Прошел Read Dead Redemption 2. Проходил я на старом пк, на виндоус мать его 7 (хотя игра на нём идти не должна, спасибо святым пиратам), на самых низких настройках графики с текстуми как на пс 2, благо догадался как поставить нормальное разрегение, а то играл бы на 1280x720. По началу мне казалось, что rdr 2 мне нравиться больше даже чем ведьмак 3, однако проходя всё дальше я начал замечать, что rdr 2 вовсе не игра. И проблема даже не в большом количестве кинематографичных катсцен и количества сюжета в игре в целом, сам геймплей в rdr 2 на самом деле не геймплей, а лишь способ игрока посмотреть кинцо на экране. Rdr 2 всячески пытается обмануть тебя и заставить поверить, что является полноценной игрой с геймплеем, а не игрокинцом и непросветлённый игрок мог бы спокойно дать себя обмануть. Однако, в какой-то момент ты понимаешь, что каждый твой выстрел это не геймплей, это лишь триггер, который запускает еще одну маленькую внутриигровую катсцену. Особенно ты это понимаешь. когда замечаешь, что ты практически неуязвим в этой игре, так как ловишь каждый замес свинцовый дождь и можешь носить с собой чуть ли не перманентный запас хила, который действует мгновенно и хиляет на полную. Так что же такое rdr 2? Red dead redemption 2 это самая настоящая разновидность жанра игрокино, того самого в котором находятся такие игры как the wolf among us, heavy rain и другие. Таким образом, я буду давать оценку этой игре исключительно в рамках жанра игрокино. Теперь про само кино: оно великолепно, возможно это до сих пор самая крутая и кинематографичная история поданная через призму игры. Наконец-то rockstar полностью избавились от клоунады в основном сюжете и создали драму с нулевым процентом клоунады, так присущей компании rockstar. Однако есть свои недостатки - игра слишком длинная, можно было просто вырезать всю часть на тропическом острове и стало бы только лучше, таким титанам как я плевать на такую продолжительность, но я уверен, многие просто бросили игру во второй половине и всё. Rdr 2 определенно самая лучшая игра в сеттинге вестерна и (на мой взгляд) лучшая игра rockstar в принципе, это то к чему они росли всю свою жизнь. Музыка великолепная, очень атмосферная, к режиссуре 0 вопросов. Несмотря на самые низкие настройки я все равно насладился визуалом. Мир игры огромен, тут есть чем заняться. Люди, которые решали пройти игру на платину, тратили на прохождение несколько сотен часов и были очень довольны. Однако, весь этот открытый мир в rdr 2 тоже к геймплею отношения не имеет, ты лишь растягиваешь кино, так как геймплейной необходимости делать хотя бы одно дополнительное действие вне основного сюжета нет вообще. Всю игру можно пройти с самым обыкновенным изначальным револьвером, не заимев при этом никаких трудностей вообще, и это еще на пк вам придется целится во врагов и что-то делать геймплейное. На консолях и геймпаде игра выглядит следующим образом: зажал кнопку прицеливания - персонаж сам прицелился на врага далее нажал кнопку выстрела, повторил это тысячу раз и игра пройдена. Всё что вы делаете вне основного сюжета просто не нужно, вы делаете это ради очередного кинца. Но несмотря на все перечисленные минусы, если принять за факт и смириться с тем, что ты играешь в кино, это великолепно - 9/10, хотя иногда всё таки очень хочется немного геймплея...

author: Zuzuwywyq
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2: A Masterpiece of Interactive Storytelling

Red Dead Redemption 2 is not just a game; it’s an extraordinary experience that redefines the potential of interactive entertainment. From its sprawling, meticulously crafted world to its deeply emotional, character-driven narrative, Rockstar Games has set an unparalleled standard in open-world design.

At its core, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a tale of loyalty, survival, and the inevitable march of progress. Set against the breathtaking backdrop of the American frontier, the game tells the story of Arthur Morgan, a hardened outlaw struggling with his place in a rapidly changing world. What makes the narrative so compelling is not just the quality of writing or the strength of its performances—though both are exceptional—but the way it makes you feel truly connected to its characters. Through every choice and interaction, you are given the opportunity to shape Arthur’s journey, creating a bond with him that lasts long after the credits roll.

The world of Red Dead Redemption 2 is one of the most detailed and immersive environments ever seen in a video game. Every inch of the map is a visual masterpiece, from the snow-capped mountains to the dense forests and rolling plains. The game’s weather system, dynamic day-night cycle, and subtle environmental details (like the rustling of leaves or the distant call of an animal) create a world that feels alive in a way that few other games manage to achieve.

The attention to detail extends to the game’s mechanics, which are equally immersive. Every interaction, whether it’s riding a horse, engaging in combat, or conversing with NPCs, feels deliberate and impactful. The gameplay encourages patience and observation, rewarding players who take the time to soak in the surroundings and engage with the world in meaningful ways. From fishing to hunting, playing poker to caring for your horse, every system is finely tuned and offers layers of depth for players to explore.

The voice acting and performances are second to none. Roger Clark’s portrayal of Arthur Morgan gives the character a raw, emotional depth that resonates throughout the game. The supporting cast, including the likes of Dutch, John, and Sadie, add further richness to the narrative, each with their own motivations and stories that weave seamlessly into the main plot. The relationships between the characters evolve organically, making every emotional high and low feel earned.

On the technical front, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a marvel. The game runs smoothly across platforms, with incredibly realistic animations, stunning lighting effects, and a soundscape that immerses players into its world. The music, composed by Woody Jackson and others, perfectly complements the tone of the story, evoking the spirit of classic Westerns while adding a unique, atmospheric layer that lingers long after you’ve put the controller down.

Finally, Red Dead Redemption 2 stands out not just for its grandeur but for its soul. It’s a game that asks players to reflect on the human condition: the complexities of morality, the pull of destiny, and the cost of living a life outside the law. It’s a haunting meditation on the end of an era and the choices we make along the way.

In every way, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a triumph—a perfect storm of storytelling, gameplay, and technical achievement that cements Rockstar’s legacy as one of the most innovative developers in the world. Simply put, it is a modern gaming classic.

A never ending mediocre horse-back riding diarrhea **** that just won't end. author: something420
text:
This game delivers a truly remarkable experience, with plenty of highlights that showcase the best of what the industry has to offer. The gunplay is immensely satisfying, particularly when using Deadeye, which makes every firefight feel cinematic and intense. The story, however, is where this game truly shines. Everything—the writing, voice acting, characters, and overarching plot—is top-tier. Special recognition goes to Arthur Morgan, who is arguably one of the best video game protagonists I’ve ever had the pleasure of playing as. His depth and relatability anchor the entire narrative. The soundtrack is another standout feature, beautifully complementing the setting and immersing you in the game’s world. Speaking of immersion, the graphics are stunning and feel ahead of their time. Released in 2018, the visuals still hold up impressively against modern titles like *Baldur's Gate 3* and *Helldivers 2*. The world-building is further enhanced by random encounters, which breathe life into the environment and make it feel truly lived-in. 

However, the game is not without its frustrations. Despite its mature rating, the gameplay often feels overly restrictive, treating players as if they need constant hand-holding. Missions are extremely linear, punishing players who think outside the box. A glaring example is the final mission with Arthur Morgan, where killing Micah prematurely results in an instant game over. This rigidity is a hallmark of modern Rockstar games, but it remains frustrating nonetheless. The game’s commitment to realism, while admirable, can make it feel sluggish at times. Actions that prioritize realism over player convenience sometimes disrupt the flow of the gameplay. The side missions also began to feel like a chore for me after a certain point. The main missions provide more than enough money to get whatever you need, making most side content feel unnecessary. The wanted system is another sore spot—it feels completely broken and inconsistent. Additionally, while the camp is a central feature of the story, it ultimately feels like it doesn’t matter in the grand scheme of things. This lack of meaningful impact diminishes what could have been a more engaging mechanic. Finally, the Guarma section in Chapter 5 feels like an unnecessary filler. If it were cut entirely, the overall story wouldn’t change much, save for a few minor details.

In conclusion, this game often feels like an interactive movie, for better or worse. Its storytelling, characters, and immersive world are nothing short of spectacular, but the linearity and occasional design missteps can make it feel constraining. Despite its flaws, it remains a must-play for anyone who appreciates cinematic gaming experiences.

author: kiozen
text: *Red Dead Redemption 2* is a masterful work of storytelling and immersion, transporting players to the American Wild West in the late 1800s with an unprecedented level of detail. The game follows the journey of Arthur Morgan, a member of Dutch van der Linde’s gang, offering a profound exploration of moral dilemmas and the hardships of an outlaw’s life. The story is rich and compelling, populated by well-written, multifaceted characters that add depth to every interaction and **** game world is vast and vibrant, showcasing breathtaking landscapes that range from snow-capped mountains to arid deserts and bustling, growing towns. Every detail of the environment is meticulously crafted, and interactions with wildlife and secondary characters contribute to a strong sense of authenticity. Game mechanics reflect the harsh realities of the era, with elements like horse management, food, and equipment care adding realism and **** gameplay strikes a balance between gunfights, exploration, and social interactions, offering both main missions and a wealth of side activities. Players enjoy a broad sense of freedom, choosing their actions and behaviors, which in turn affect their honor and relationships within the world. The soundtrack is equally memorable, featuring compositions that perfectly blend with the story’s melancholic, wild **** essence, *Red Dead Redemption 2* is a captivating and immersive experience, delivering an epic, reflective journey into the complexities of life on the frontier.

author: MaykeLovin
text:
Aqui estão alguns pontos notáveis que fazem deste jogo uma experiência inesquecível:

Direção e Personagens: Uma Perspectiva Autêntica

 A direção do jogo é verdadeiramente incrível. Cada personagem tem sua própria voz e perspectiva sobre os acontecimentos. Você sente que está imerso em um mundo onde cada indivíduo tem uma história a contar. Desde o grandioso e melhor protagonista de todos os tempos, Arthur Morgan, até os coadjuvantes, todos têm profundidade e complexidade. ( Bjz Sadie)

Gráficos e Atmosfera: Beleza no Mundo Aberto

Embora Red Dead Redemption 2 possa não ter as texturas mais fotorealistas do mercado, ele compensa com uma atmosfera deslumbrante. Os cenários são de tirar o fôlego, desde as vastas planícies até as montanhas cobertas de neve. O jogo captura a essência do Velho Oeste de maneira magistral, com cenas que variam de momentos de calmaria a tiroteios intensos.

Narrativa Impactante: Lágrimas e Emoções

A história é um dos pontos altos. Ela se desenrola de forma gradual, permitindo que você se conecte profundamente com os personagens e suas jornadas. Lembro-me de momentos em que me vi emocionalmente envolvido, chorando muito durante uma missão ou alguma animação in gameplay. Essa conexão é rara em jogos de mundo aberto.

O Prológo: Uma Pequena Mancha em um Quadro Brilhante 

Embora necessário para estabelecer a trama, ele pode parecer um pouco longo e lento para alguns jogadores.

author: sabbattousai
text:
"I gave you all I had"

From the moment Arthur Morgan steps onto the sun-drenched plains of the late 19th-century American frontier, Red Dead Redemption 2 is more than just a game; it’s a journey into a world that feels as alive and untamed as the wild lands it portrays. Having spent 74 hours immersed in this masterpiece, I can confidently say that the experience was as unforgettable as the tales of the Old West itself.Rockstar Games has created a vast epic that, at its heart, tells the deeply human story of Arthur Morgan—a character whose depth and development set new standards for protagonists in video games. Arthur is not merely a rugged outlaw; he is a man struggling with his past, the burden of his decisions, and the disintegrating world around him. His story unfolds with an authenticity that is both moving and inspiring, leaving a lasting mark on anyone who engages with it.What truly sets Red Dead Redemption 2 apart is its commitment to realism and immersion. From the rustling leaves in a dense forest to the distant sound of a train whistle, every sound and sight adds to a captivating sense of place. The game’s attention to detail is apparent in every corner of its expansive world, making it a marvel of interactive storytelling.Additionally, the soundtrack of Red Dead Redemption 2 is nothing short of exceptional. The musical score, including the hauntingly beautiful "Unshaken," perfectly complements the game’s atmosphere and narrative. It deepens the emotional impact of key moments and enhances the overall experience, leaving players with a lasting impression long after the game is **** conclusion, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a triumph of storytelling and design. It challenges the boundaries of the medium, offering an experience that is both grand in scale and intimate in its portrayal of the human condition. For those seeking an adventure that is as deep as it is breathtaking, this game is a must-play.Pros:Deep character development, especially for Arthur MorganStunning and immersive worldRich storytellingVaried and dynamic gameplay experiencesExceptional soundtracks, including the standout track "Unshaken".

Rating: 9/10

author: Sventibaldo
text:
A fun game overall, but extremely overrated. Definitely not a masterpiece. Story is engaging, but it takes itself too seriously and it has many nonsensical, cartoonish moments. Overall the writing is subpar, but the dialogues are good and the acting is excellent.
The game suffers from way too many issues to be considered great. Controls are awful and gameplay design is extremely poor. All missions are the same and the game forces you to strictly follow a script every step of the away, taking away all player's freedom.
There are a lot of boring moments and overall the world, while beautifully crafted, is rather empty and not that big either. Towns in particular are very small and unimpressive.
Side missions are also very lackluster.
The best thing in this games are the animals and hunting. Unfortunately i hate hunting, but if you love killing squirrels and skinning them, this game is for you.
Interactions with the world and its characters are also pretty dull.
A lot of efforts have been put towards immersion, with some results, but overall i could never get really immersed, due to the childish plot and completely unrealistic mechanics, like the whole crime system, which is awful with police teleporting all over the places and ridiculous bounty system which allows you to commit mass murder and then clear your criminal record by simply paying 100 dollars to the nearest post **** immersive!

author: SwabGames
text: This game was recommended to me by a friend of mine who completed it before me and gave me a couple of instructions on it. When I was able to buy it, I immediately installed it, and when the game was launched, I immediately joined it. I went through every quest, watched every cut-scene, and went through the main plot with great interest. And when I finished the game, I realized why this game is so loved - the non-linear plot. And, as a person who has completed this game twice, I can describe all the pros and cons of this game. Let's start with the positives. This game has a very large open world, with many locations, cities, even landscapes. This game also boasts an excellent plot and well-developed main characters. A very non-linear plot, which differs from most games and on which many theories can be built, which is seasoned on the one hand with absolutely understandable main characters, but if you think about it... I especially liked the development of Arthur as a character, first as a bandit, ready to give everything for the sake of his gang, and then, as a lost leader who saw the disintegration of the gang, he tries to at least somehow “atone” for the sins of the person. Another plus is the diverse flora and fauna. Since the game has many forms of landscape, fields, forests, lakes, hills and mountains, there are correspondingly many different animals and plants. When I played the game for the first time, I was a little freaked out by such variety. Even after completing the plot and ending, I played another 30 hours just like that, driving the entire map in search of new game or animal to sell skins. But the downside, as another friend of mine told me, is that the game is too slow, especially at the beginning. Deep down I agree with him, I sometimes caught myself thinking this way, but I still liked the game. Well, as a result, I can say that this game, it seems to me, has forever become top 1 on my list of favorite games.

author: LigmiBalls
text: Red Dead Redemption 2* is a masterclass in storytelling, world-building, and gameplay, making it one of the most remarkable achievements in gaming history. Developed by Rockstar Games, this open-world epic immerses players in the final days of the American Wild West, delivering an experience that is as gripping as it is expansive.**Story and Characters:**The narrative of *Red Dead Redemption 2* is its crown jewel. Set in 1899, the game follows Arthur Morgan, a member of the Van der Linde gang, as he grapples with loyalty, morality, and survival. The story is rich and complex, filled with deeply human characters that evolve over time. Arthur's journey is poignant, and his interactions with other gang members—like the charismatic yet flawed Dutch Van der Linde—create a narrative tapestry that is both emotionally charged and thought-provoking.**World and Atmosphere:**The game's world is nothing short of breathtaking. From the snowy peaks of the Grizzlies to the murky swamps of Lemoyne, each environment is meticulously crafted with attention to detail. The world feels alive, with dynamic weather, realistic wildlife, and towns brimming with life. Every corner of the map holds a story, be it an abandoned cabin or a random encounter with a stranger. The level of immersion is unparalleled, making the world of *Red Dead Redemption 2* feel both vast and intimate.**Gameplay:**Gameplay in *Red Dead Redemption 2* is robust and varied. The mechanics are deep, offering players a wide range of activities, from hunting and fishing to engaging in intense gunfights. The game's controls can feel deliberate, which may take some getting used to, but this pace adds to the realism. The Honor system, which tracks your actions and influences how the world reacts to you, adds a layer of moral complexity to your decisions.**Visuals and Sound:**Visually, the game is a marvel. The graphics are stunning, with incredible attention to detail in character models, landscapes, and lighting. The sound design is equally impressive, with a soundtrack that perfectly complements the game's tone and setting. From the rustling of leaves to the distant howl of a wolf, every sound adds to the atmosphere, drawing you further into the world.**Conclusion:***Red Dead Redemption 2* is not just a game; it's an experience. Its rich narrative, compelling characters, and immersive world set a new standard for open-world games. While its pacing and controls might not be for everyone, those who stick with it will find a game that rewards patience and exploration. It's a tale of the Wild West that will stay with you long after the credits roll. Simply put, *Red Dead Redemption 2* is a masterpiece.

author: SPECTER-21
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 en PC ha demostrado ser el pináculo en términos técnicos y narrativos, sin duda uno de los juegos más destacados que he tenido el placer de jugar.Este juego no se conforma con menos: está repleto de detalles minuciosos y su mundo se siente increíblemente vivo. Montar a caballo a través del vasto mapa es una experiencia única, ya sea por los impresionantes paisajes o las sorpresas ocultas que te esperan a lo largo del camino. Los encuentros con personajes necesitados o eventos aleatorios añaden una capa adicional de **** historia es una maravilla en sí misma. El progreso de los personajes y el modo en que están desarrollados es simplemente magistral por parte de Rockstar. Aunque no jugué al Red Dead Redemption 1, es innegable que Arthur Morgan se convierte en un favorito instantáneo. La trama en su conjunto es emocionante y, evitando cualquier spoiler, el final logró un nivel de impacto emocional que raramente experimento en los **** resumen, Red Dead Redemption 2 es una obra maestra que abarca todos los aspectos. Aunque su único punto negativo podría ser que algunos logros requieren jugar en línea, esta es una pequeña mancha en una experiencia de juego que brilla por sí misma. Si eres un fan de la saga o simplemente buscas un juego que combine una narrativa impactante con un mundo expansivo y detallado, este título es una joya que merece un lugar especial en tu colección.

author: alvarocortess
text: Bueno esta es la tercera vez que me paso rdr2 y no tengo palabras para describir la grandeza que tiene este titulo y lo que consigue hacer Rockstar con esta obra. Este juego no es un simple juego lo considero mas una experiencia que todos deberían de vivir al menos una vez. Esta claro que el juego es lento pero es necesario que el juego sea así para enseñarte todo lo que ofrece y poder de esa forma disfrutarlo como es debido. Desde como se ve, que es una completa barbaridad teniendo en cuenta que estamos hablando de un juego de 2018 y que a día de hoy en 2024 muy pocos juegos consiguen hacerle frente de tu a tu, desde lo bien que va en cualquier plataforma que lo corras (en Pc tiene una optimización brutal) desde su gameplay (par algunas personas repetitivo) pero sinceramente no se como podrían haberle dado mas profundidad a disparar teniendo n cuenta que no deja de ser un sandbox, su estructura de misiones otro de los puntos que mucha gente ha criticado del titulo y de verdad que me lo he pasado tres veces y considero que red dead te pone en un montón de situaciones muy diversas y que para nada en  las 7p u 80 horas que le puedes dedicar se te puede hacer repetitivo. Todo esto acompañado de hasta el momento el mejor mundo abierto que se ha creado en la historia de la industria. Con un millón de cosas por hacer, npcs que realmente tienen una vida detrás y no están ahí simplemente por estar, cada ciudad como puede ser (Valentine, Rhodes, Saint Denis, Blackwater, Strawberry, Van horn...) tiene su encanto y su diseño artístico, su gente que actúan de manera diferente en fin se nota que estas realmente en lugares diferentes, Y que decir de la historia para mi una de las mejores historias creadas en la industria con unos personajes fascinantes (Habría que hacerle una reseña solamente al personaje de Dutch) y llevada por lo que para es el mejor protagonista jamás escrito en la historia, Arthur Morgan, con Arthur vivimos una verdadera redención que realmente nos lleva a plantearnos cosas y llegamos a vivir momentos muy felices y momentos muy trágicos, es complicado de explicar lo dentro que se te puede llegar a meter Arthur pero no es un simple personaje de un juego mas, sino que llega a ser alguien al que realmente le cogemos un cariño especial. Para ir terminando simplemente lo dicho me parece una de las mejores experiencias que puedes vivir jugando a videojuegos y si tuviera que decir algo malo es que hay veces que el personaje se queda un poco atorado debido a la gran cantidad de mecánicas que tiene si se queda una superpuesta de la otra pero quitando esa tontearía solamente tengo palabras de admiración hacia Rockstar por haber creado esta carta de amor a los videojuegos.

Le scénario n'arrange rien et ne relève pas le niveau , on est sur du western série B avec tous les poncifs du genre , bien loin des qualités d'un jeu comme the Witcher par exemple .
Rien n'est intuitif , même pas les touches de commande , on passe plus de temps à comprendre pourquoi ce foutu cheval  se met à courir ou pas , comme le personnage , à ramasser tout un tas de trucs sans intérêt si ce n'est de rallonger la durée de jeu  et l'ennui qu'il procure ...

Le jeu ne vaut pas le prix qu'il coûte .

author: BossDoug
text: In the vast expanse of gaming, few titles manage to capture the essence of an entire era, a spirit of adventure, and a sense of belonging quite like Red Dead Redemption 2. From the moment you step foot into its meticulously crafted world, you're transported to a time when the Wild West wasn't just a setting, but a way of life. Rockstar Games has outdone themselves with this magnum opus, delivering an experience that transcends mere entertainment and becomes an unforgettable journey through the heart of America's untamed frontier.Passionate doesn't even begin to describe the relationship I have with this game. It's an obsession, a love affair that deepens with every sunrise over the plains, every thunderstorm rolling across the sky, and every encounter with its richly developed characters. Arthur Morgan isn't just a protagonist; he's a legend in his own right, a flawed yet undeniably human figure whose story resonates long after the final credits roll.this game doesnt deserve the bad meta score of 97 it desererves 100 and no negative reviews this game is beyong good and would give it a 11 in score if i could. From the breathtaking landscapes of the open world to the intricate details of its bustling towns and settlements, every inch of Red Dead Redemption 2 feels alive. It's a testament to Rockstar's dedication to their craft, a commitment to immersion that sets a new standard for open-world gaming. Whether you're hunting game in the wilderness, robbing trains under the cover of night, or simply sitting around a campfire swapping stories with your fellow outlaws, there's always something new to discover, something to marvel at in this living, breathing world.

author: derealization
text:
I didn't love much western style. The western movies was not really good for me due to the setting. That is because all western movies/games and other piece of artwork are a bit stereoperized. Horses, revolvers, cowboy hats, boots, saloons - this is peculiarities of western, no one shows the truth of living in this times, all they show how cowboys are cool, with gang, killing people, riding horses and hanging out in saloon. But Red Dead Redemption 2 was something different i guess from the start. Firstly, we used to know that we lost three members of gang: Jenny, Mac and Shawn. It was the first thing that catches my mind to that game, now i started to think like "Isn't this a game that idealizes the nomadic lifestyle of the wild west?". After ending first chapter game to fourth was to me not so interesting, so i left a game for later, leaving it on PS4, PC 2 times. And now, after finishing that game like 20 mins ago, i decided to write the review(even made account on metacritic, because steam don't appreciate a long reviews). That's the first game of my 7 year gaming experience that really woken my emotions to the characters. I almost cried on Arthur's Death, was very happy for John when he asks Abigail is she want to marry him. I feel like i'm controlling book main character. And after the main character dies, i just buy a book with continuation, but with other character. 
                                      My opinion about the game.
I'll start with the plot. Like i said before, the game wakes my emotions and really felt emotions as same as characters. Every human(can't say otherwise due to looking so real) is written so damn well, so if you want to learn some characters history - go check wiki of RDR2. The backstory of Arthur is really so hella desperate, he lost mom at 11 and seen his father hangs myself. He lost wife with a kid for a **** 10 dollars, and if this was happen in real life, i think most of men just killed himself. Because what is the point of life, when you lost the most dear thing due to a **** piece of paper? So Arthur joined a gang with Dutch, where the business at start goes quite good, but at the end there is something that broke Arthur itself. He knew he can't live a life like that, die as a outlaw. Some people are arguing who is Arthur really is: the good man or a just regular outlaw, who tries to lie down. In my opinion this persona neither good or bad man. I mean, he seen too much in his life, can't control himself due to chaos in mind. The man dies unhappily at his 35s or something, without making a family or making mileage to society. Too much homeless people who needs help, Arthur could make them live good life with all his robbed money, but all of this goes to John(who don't know, all money at the end of the game, in the cabin was robbed cash with Arthur, and some from Blackwater also). I feel happy for the John, he finally gets happy with his life, living in a owned ranch, having a family, kid, money and all needed stuff. I think Arthur dies for John's interests, because he was too old to make a new family, so he tried to help John. Dies as a hero to John.
About the gameplay - for someone it seems boring, but for me is ideally best pace for a storyteller game like this. It's not a **** Marvel where too much action for ADHD fans, who can't last 3 hours for watching a movie with deep story and idea.
The graphics is mindblowing for 2018, even tho this game have graphic mods, which made this game even better.
I'm thinking that is the end of my review, i can't tell about this masterpiece so much, play the game if you didn't(i'm doubting it, normal personas don't read spoiler reviews). I will end this game completing it too 100%, with all achievements(aaahhhh i **** hate RDO achievements, the online in game is boring tbh), so if you want to check my progress of achievements - my steam is de_realization.Thanks for reading it, too much text anyway, have a nice day :)

author: TwoBe
text:
Despite not being a fan of cowboy themes, Red Dead Redemption II managed to rope me in and keep me thoroughly engaged. 

The game stands out for its incredible storytelling and character development, making it easy to get attached to many of the characters. Arthur, in particular, shines as a protagonist, offering depth and complexity that's rare in video games. However, Abigail's portrayal struck a discordant note, coming across as excessively obnoxious, which might have been the writers' intention, but it felt overdone.

The voice acting deserves a special mention for bringing the characters to life, complemented by a soundtrack and graphics that immerse you in its world. 

While the gameplay is solid overall, it does suffer from moments of clunkiness that can detract from the experience. Nonetheless, the amazing story and overall presentation make Red Dead Redemption II a memorable journey through the Wild West.

author: Jquist47
text: It is without a doubt the most overrated game of all time, considering the reviews and general praise the game gets. The story is a complete mess overall. The story is essentially about a gang of outlaws or criminals that attempts to gather enough money so they can live independently in some sort of paradise life. You are playing as degenerate, that thinks they have the moral high ground by robbing rich (and poor) and then distributing it to your fellow gang members. How is that fun, or how is that a good story? Not to mention the story itself isn't gripping in the slightest. There is no clear objective or incentivizing moment in the story to make the player understand or actually care about the gang or it's characters. there is no cohesion, sense of direction and focus in the story to make the player actually engaged in it. The writing is nothing special, the dialogue between the characters is extraordinarily uninteresting, none of them have anything interesting to say and neverreveal any interesting backstory. The incredibly dull characters in the camp are somewhat fleshing out through side content and camp wandering, but not only was that overly tedious that I never wanted to do it, but largely uninteresting because getting piecemeal insights on forgettable camp follower isn't compelling as they weren't introduced well to begin with. Gameplay is quite poor and considering how long the game is, the gameplay never evolves. You don't unlock new skills, abilities or anything (like you would in a true rpg) the only progression is unlocking new weapons and clothing, which have minimal gameplay impact. So the gameplay from the first min is going to be roughly the same as your end-game gameplay, which is alsovery boring. The graphics and open world is good, but thats not enough to carry the game. All the open world activities are pointless, so the incentive to explore and adventure out in the open world quickly diminishes. Despite this, it is often regarded as the best game of all time, I wonder if these people are generally unintelligent/haven't played many games or if there is something I don't get about this game.

text: Red Dead Redemption 2 is an exceptional game that brilliantly captures the essence of the Wild West. Its attention to detail creates an immersive world, from expansive landscapes to intricate towns and characters. The storyline is a true masterpiece, delving into themes of redemption, loyalty, and the harsh realities of the era.Completing the narrative leaves a lasting impact, with a sense of accomplishment and emotional resonance. The character development, especially for Arthur Morgan, adds significant depth to the overall experience, allowing players to fully inhabit the characters.Scoring a perfect 10/10, Red Dead Redemption 2 excels in storytelling, world-building, and innovative gameplay. It sets a new standard for open-world gaming, making it a challenge to find a title that rivals its excellence. Undoubtedly, it stands as the pinnacle of my gaming experiences, showcasing the incredible heights the medium can achieve.

author: BHRipper
text:
One of the best games ever made.

It manages to tell a compelling story with tremendously believable characters all while being a technical marvel. The game's astonishing graphics and open world are unmatched even 5 years into its lifetime, and the level of polish it has in every aspect shows the tremendous hard work the team put into making this masterpiece.

Gameplay, pacing, and mission structure might not be for everyone and for sure it's something they could've improved on, but it has so much more well-made content to offer that it doesn't subtract much to the overall experience of the game.

Also, there's no next gen console version, and the PC version hasn't got the treatment it deserves by Rockstar Games, but I see that more of a company issue than the game itself.

Overall, it's a magical experience that I will always recommend to anyone.

author: emike09
text:
Hands down the best game I've ever played in my 38 years of life. I'm wrapping up my 5th playthrough. This is my #1 go-to game when I can't think of what else to play.

The visuals are incredible. I've added some small visual mods to enhance textures and atmosphere, but even vanilla, it's astounding. Playing on a 4090 at 4k HDR. It's the atmospheres that really get me. Watching the sun's rays march through a foggy east-coast morning, heavy clouds rolling in before a moody cold storm hits, watching the sun set over a lake while fishing as birds fly around and a mountain lion sneaks up behind me. 

The world is incredibly alive. The trees sway in the wind realistically, animals are everywhere, NPCs can attack out of nowhere. There are so many tiny attentions to detail. Even after 5 playthroughs, I'm still discovering new things.

My only complaint is that there isn't more story. The story is huge and there's a thousand hours of things to do, but I want more! It's sad I'll probably be in my late 40s when/if the next version comes out.

author: Dustymetso
text: Red Dead Redemption 2 for PC stands as a triumph in many aspects, offering a meticulously optimized experience, captivating narrative, stunning graphics, and unparalleled freedom within its open-world environment. Rockstar Games' masterpiece delivers an immersive Wild West experience, enabling players to traverse an exquisitely detailed landscape while engaging in diverse activities like hunting, side missions, and exploration. The optimization for the PC version of Red Dead Redemption 2 is commendable. The game runs smoothly, showcasing its visually breathtaking landscapes and lifelike character details without compromising performance. The beauty of its graphics, from the sprawling landscapes to the minute details, creates an immersive world that's a visual feast for players. One of its strongest attributes lies in its free roam mechanics. The ability to engage in various activities like hunting, side missions, and item collection adds depth to the gameplay. Exploring the vast open world is a joy, with countless treasures to discover and experiences to be had. However, despite its many strengths, the game suffers from a relatively linear and dated design philosophy, which significantly affects the overall experience. The game's structured missions often lead players down a predetermined path, restricting the freedom that the open world otherwise promises. The rigid "go here, do this" nature of missions and the lack of flexibility can feel restrictive and counterintuitive in a game that boasts an expansive world. The game's adherence to a cinematic style contributes to its linear design, sometimes stifling player agency. The stringent mission objectives that penalize deviation limit the organic exploration and player choice, causing frustration for those seeking a more open-ended experience akin to older titles like Deus Ex, which offered more freedom in decision-making. In summary, Red Dead Redemption 2 for PC is a visually stunning and narratively captivating game that excels in many areas. However, its adherence to a more linear design philosophy limits player agency and contradicts the open-world nature that defines its appeal. While its cinematic approach enhances storytelling, it comes at the cost of player freedom, which might disappoint those seeking a more flexible and choice-driven experience. Despite these limitations, Red Dead Redemption 2 remains a remarkable achievement in gaming, blending stunning visuals, compelling storytelling, and an expansive world that, while somewhat constrained, still offers an unforgettable journey through the American frontier.

author: GalaxxyKiller
text:
Starting with the many good points that this beautiful game has, the depth of the environment, a wide variety of animals, plants, easter eggs, beautiful landscapes where you just want to be there in your camp appreciating the view and more.
The variety of things that are distributed around the map, points of interest, encounters with strangers, missions of strangers, good variety of weapons that you will discover in the course of the playthrough, mini games like poker, black jack, dominoes, theaters and more things that are distributed on the map.
I could go on with the good points that are in the game but this review could be very long.
Bad points: Fast travel at the beginning of the game, although as such there is the possibility of fast travel (buying a map for the camp or placing a camp in the wilderness and from there place the quick trip to points of interest already explored) is not like placing a marker and from there select the fast travel, you can only get close to your marker but you can't get there exactly, the first chapter can be slow but once you pass it everything will go smoothly and the story will unfold little by little, some missions are very meh but there are many missions that are very cool and you get to enjoy them.
In summary for me, this game is a 10/10 but qualifying it as a review is a 9/10 for the above mentioned.
Would I recommend this game?, of course I would, it is worth at least trying it or have it in your games to play list, there are people who say it is boring, that its gameplay is very bad and so on but it is everyone's perspective, and we are human beings and we have different opinions.
I hope this review has been useful for you and remember "Take a gamble that love exists, and do a loving act" ;)

text: Boah, this is the open world game. No, BEST GAME OF ALL TIMEVisually the most outstanding game with so much attention to details in this living and breathing world. text:
I just had the chance to play this game in 2023.

It was a really amazing experience. It is not just a game in which you do things that lead to an end, But you get to live the life of the main character, see his evolution and most importantly the evolution of the ones around him, the environment and even the small towns cities evolve through time.

author: BoobSlayer
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2 is an extraordinary gaming experience that excels in multiple aspects. One of its standout features is the impeccable attention to detail in its physics and little nuances. With each playthrough, you'll uncover new intricacies in the game world that truly enhance immersion. Whether it's the way snow realistically deforms under your horse's hooves or the delicate animations of wildlife, it's clear that Rockstar went above and beyond to create a lifelike environment.

The game's story is nothing short of great, weaving a gripping narrative that keeps players engaged from start to finish. While it's true that some parts of the story can feel lengthy, these slower moments serve to build the tension and ultimately add to the grand climax. The character development and intricate relationships within the Van der Linde gang contribute to the emotional depth of the narrative, making it a truly memorable journey.

Voice acting and visuals in Red Dead Redemption 2 are nothing short of breathtaking. The characters' voices are rich with emotion, and the performances truly bring them to life. The game's visuals are stunning, from the sprawling landscapes of the Wild West to the meticulous character models and animations. Every aspect of the game's presentation is a testament to the dedication of the development team.

In summary, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a masterpiece that excels in physics, attention to detail, storytelling, voice acting, and visuals. While it may have moments that test your patience, these only serve to heighten the overall experience. It's a game that continues to reveal its beauty and complexity with each playthrough, making it a must-play title for any gamer.

author: Sergius_Grey
text:
I've started playing this game six times, including when I bought it on PS5.
Each time something prevented me from playing more than the end of the first act.
But all my friends kept telling me that it was a good game and worth trying again.
And so the time came when I said to myself - either I need to put on my hat, check my revolvers and find out which way Arthur Morgan will go and where he will end up in the end, or never start the said game again.
And as you can imagine, I wouldn't be writing this review if I chose the second option.
What I mean is, if there are guys and girls who, like me, have not been hooked by the game from the first hours of the game, do not give up and throw Red Dead Redemption 2 into a dark corner, give the game a chance, and somewhere after a third of the passage, the game will fully thank you for it with unexpected plot twists, deeper disclosure of the main characters of the game, "chemistry" between the characters, and so on. In general, the game is big, looks and sounds good, is filled with various references, and you want to explore it.
If you are a fan of the Wild West, then this will be a 10 out of 10 hit for you.
That's all for now. Have a good day and enjoy your coffee.

author: unwaten
text:
Red Dead Redemption 2: Captivating World with Gameplay Inconsistencies"

Red Dead Redemption 2 is considered a masterpiece that stands out with its details, atmosphere, and deep story within the gaming world. However, alongside these remarkable features, there are also some gameplay-related issues that are noticeable.

Positive Aspects:

Visual Spectacle: The game's graphics and level of detail incredibly portray the western-themed world. The beauty of nature, the liveliness of towns, and character animations are truly impressive.

Deep Story: The story of Red Dead Redemption 2 pulls players in with character developments and impactful storytelling. Arthur Morgan's dramatic journey and the downfall of the Van der Linde gang allow players to emotionally connect.

Open World Exploration: Offering players freedom in a vast world, the game provides an immersive life simulation experience through activities like hunting and fishing.

Negative Aspects:

Gameplay Issues: The game's slow-paced gameplay might bother some players. Long journeys and the slowness of character animations can sometimes make the experience feel tedious.

Artificial Intelligence Problems: Limited reactions and behavioral patterns of NPCs undermine the realism of the world. As a result, interactions can sometimes feel predictable and artificial.

Mission Design: Certain missions can tire players due to unnecessary repetitions or long journeys. Additionally, the uneven difficulty level among missions can diminish players' motivation.

In conclusion, Red Dead Redemption 2 offers a captivating experience with its visual spectacle, deep story, and open-world exploration. However, the gameplay's sluggishness, artificial intelligence issues, and certain mission design shortcomings can cast a shadow over the player's experience. Alongside these aspects, the game still continues to provide an unforgettable experience for those who wish to explore its magnificent world.

author: TheBasilisKK
text:
First of all, the game is not perfect. No game is. But it's really goddam close.

Pros:
The characters are acted better than any other game ever, and the story is dynamic and gives the player so much freedom (not RPG levels but you know). The world feels so alive, and almost every NPC can be interacted with. Every tree and rock feels like it is there for a reason, and the cities and towns have incredible atmosphere and feel like they exist in real life. The game looks amazing as well (at launch it was really buggy and badly optimized but now it's one of the best optimized games on Steam. I have a laptop with an RTX 3050 in it and on medium to high settings, it gets 50-60fps in most places and drops to 40-50 in the larger towns and cities.)

Cons:
Controls feel like they are 10 years old (probably because they are. Its essentially the same as Red Dead 1). They feel very sluggish and unresponsive. Your horse will often stop and spin in a circle if you try to turn too much while sprinting on it. The gunplay is pretty good but not great and the game isn't very difficult, it just adds difficulty by throwing a bunch of enemies at you. Even so, I still die a lot more from the bad controls than from the enemies actually being that hard (and no, there are no difficulty options. You are stuck with what the game gives you).

text: RDR2 initially took some time to captivate me, but as I continued playing, I found myself genuinely enjoying the experience. author: famas
text:
Really disappointing nothing really feels like it was ready for release. For me personally the performance is OK 60+ fps on balanced settings with 6700K and a GTX 1070.

Most of my complaints are just with the bugs and lost freedom of the game. I have a problem where the mouse aiming is not very precise and when trying to make small adjustments to line up shots it is almost impossible because the reticle moves in 5-6 pixels at a time and has almost like a deadzone for how much the mouse has to move before it registers (Like the problem that still persists with the GTA IV pc port).
When looking back at other games Rockstar have released it was hoping for the aiming and combat to be atleast as good as previous games like GTA 5 or Max Payne 3. But no, it feels clunky and imprecise.
Movement also aint so good. Trying to walk close to a ledge to push some over? Too bad Arthur has a death wish and jumps down with no hesitation. And movement just feels more restrictive compared to GTA 5, changing direction is slow and is made even worse if youre riding a horse.

One time where i realised rockstar had removed freedom was when chasing a train a promt comes up "Jump to train". But it only appears when it is clear. Why was that made? why not make me able to jump always make ME time it and if i dont i get to see Arthur ragdoll and get hurt this would make it more intense when trying to leap from your horse instead of it being precalculated it just needs me to press the button. Made me feel really sad.

Freedom in missions is also very rare youre constantly being told what to do and how to do it. Follow this man, wait for this cutscene, shoot these guys. It is VERY boring and tedius. A mission where they have to rescue Sean from a boat full of bad guys. Instead of ME, the PLAYER figuring out how to rescue him, the game does it all for me and i have no input on what happends. Might aswell watch a movie instead of these. Its like a constant cutscene but where i have to hold down 'W' to keep my horse moving forward and only the 'W' does anything, trying to turn the horse and nothing happends they strip me of my controls to make me stick to the plan but keeps me awake to make me press 'W' and bore myself to death.

The game looks and sounds incredible and i have no complaints here. But it feels like the wanted to make a movie instead ****. Most of the time youre just coasing by no doing anything because the game is doing it for you. An addition i liked more than i would have thought was the growing beard and hair. Its just a really nice feature.

Also the game crashes almost constantly if in fullscreen mode. I found that if left in fullscreen-windowed mode, it has a much lower change of crashing out of nowhere. If buying the game wait for the steam release. Steam more features and functionality compared to the rockstar launcher which was built in 2 weeks by interns being paid minimum wage.

author: mikaelus
text:
RDR2 is all that's great and all that's terrible in modern gaming bundled into a single product.

First of all, it's not really a game - it's an interactive movie where you are prompted to press buttons at a specific time, that's all. In the course of the campaign none of your choices matter - that is assuming you occasionally do get to make a choice at all.

This has become a real plague these days, probably due to influence of consoles, where controls are limited and achieving real mastery (save for a few genres) is near impossible.

Ironically, the only time you feel like you're playing a game is... when you're not playing it, just roaming around the beautiful open world. That is the best part of RDR2 - just riding around, exploring, hunting, looking for treasure before returning to the mindless campaign of pressing buttons and, sometimes, shooting bad guys in carefully choreographed scenes that you also have zero influence over.

The visuals, the atmosphere, landscapes are all phenomenal - really among the best in the open world genre. But the game as a "game" fails in every respect. You never really feel like YOU are playing but rather just ticking boxes in somebody else's scenario.

Good or evil, consequences of your actions are ultimately the same, as is the conclusion, after which you're really left with nothing to do.

I spent 100 hours on it, rather enjoyably, but also consistently frustrated that the freedom I was promised is really just a mirage and that I have absolutely no impact on anything.

You also get the sense that the project overwhelmed the Rockstar team. A good part of the map (30-40%) is pretty much locked out of the main campaign and becomes only accessible in the epilogue when you discover... there's not much to do there. It's like they tried to make something out of it but clearly got pressured by deadlines and left it for dead.

With time you also realize that crafting stuff makes little sense either and new guns that you unlock later in game don't really add anything new.

There's really no reward for advancing in either of these verticals - again, as if someone started working on it and left it half baked.

You'll do well with the first selection of the most powerful pistols and rifles, and only use the rest if it's required to hunt a specific animal. That's it.

As an open world experience, RDR2 is as good as it gets, 10/10, absolutely fantastic and thoroughly enjoyable. But as a game... well, as I said, it really isn't one. You're just a spectator occasionally asked to press a button as a way to tease you that you have any involvement at all.

It could have been something much greater.

In a way, I'd like them to continue working on it and spend the next few years making it into something it could have been.

author: ricardely
text:
Is it so difficult to make a perfect game? I dedicated 120 hours to the story on XBOX ONE S and 200 hours to the Online mode on PC, and the summary is simple: Masterpiece. Only Geralt comes close to whispering in its ear, no one else. There is no product close to this level of quality.

RDR2 has it all, a very well-crafted story, well-crafted characters, crazy graphics, absurdly immersive realism and game feeling, and an open world that actually feels full of details, unpredictable and surprising, something impossible to find in the packaged open worlds we see today. Ubisoft knows exactly what I'm talking about.

RDR2 is a huge game in size and spectacular in detail, only suitable for dedicated players (not necessarily hardcore) who are willing to dedicate the necessary time for the game to seep into them. If you are a casual gamer, I recommend titles more like Naughty Dog, with an equally well-crafted game feeling, story, and characters, but with a much simpler and linear approach.

An adult game for adult people.

author: philzlz
text:
I only started playing the single player four years after release and was impressed by how good it was. Compared to other open worlds this one feels lived in, from NPC chatter, realistic small towns and cities, the physics and weather engine to flora and fauna, it is an example of how an open world should be constructed in video games.

The story keeps you interested, characters have depth and are likeable (or not) and the game keeps you entertained for at least over 40 hours. If you want to complete everything you can easily spend over 100 hours.

With open world games feeling empty and more like a checklist full of icons that you work off one by one this is a prime example of how it should be done and deserves its place in the top 10 of the best games made to date.

author: ErayTellezi
text:
Bu oyun bana kendisinden 100 yıl sonrasında geçen Sopranos dizisini anımsattı. Sopranos'ta mafyanın altın yılları geride kalmış, yüzyılın sonu ile birlikte İtalyan gençlerin mafyaya ilgisi bittiği gibi mafya, eskiden haraç kestiği esnafın yerini kurumsal şirketler alınca zora düşmüştür. Modası geçmiştir. Aynısı tam yüz yıl önce kovboylara olmuş rdr 2 'ye göre. Ulaşımın gelişmesi medeniyeti her yana yaymış, kanun kaçaklarının saklanmasını zorlaştırmış gibi görünüyor.

Hayatımda bu kadar organik ilerleyen, yan etkinliklerini bu kadar doğal sunan, canlılığını bu kadar hissettiren bir açık dünya oyunu oynamadım. Adım attığınız her yerde oranın yaşadığını hissediyorsunuz. Kovboy simülasyonu ama dev bütçelisinden. Çok az sanat eseri bu seviyede oradaymışsın gibi hissettirebilir.

Yaptığınız küçük şeylerin dünyaya etkisini hissediyorsunuz. İnşaatına yardım ettiğiniz adamın evi tamamlanıyor mesela ama bu görev bile değil halbuki. Demiryolu inşaatının ilerlediğini görüyorsunuz. Yardım etmediğiniz bir kadının günler sonra cesedini bulabiliyorsunuz. Her köşe başında bir hikaye var. Yolda rastgele münakaşaya girdiğiniz haydutlarla kapışma şekli bile çeşitlilik gösteriyor. Kimi kasa açmaya çalışıyor, kimi arkadaşını polisin elinden kurtarıyor oluyor, kimi yolunuzu kesiyor. Dağ başında rastgele gördüğünüz bir evin önünde oturan adam sizi akşam yemeğine davet ediyor ve karısıyla beraber sizi sarhoş edip tüm paranızı çalıyorlar. Dediğim gibi bunlar görev bile değil. Bu rastgelelik sizi dünyayı keşfetmeye itiyor. Bu hissin bu kadar yoğun olduğu tek oyun Skyrim'di galiba.

Oyundaki karakterlerin hepsi nevi şahsına münhasır. Hepsi çok iyi yazılmışlar. Kimi sinir ediciliğiyle, kimi dost canlılığıyla sizin ilginizi çekiyor. Dutch'ın babacan bir lider olarak başlayıp, bencil, şan şöhret düşkünü, bu uğurda herkesi satacak bir adama dönüşmesi muhteşem işlenmiş. Micah denen yavşağın gıcıklığını yıllar geçse bile unutamam. Kamptaki diğer isimler, yan görevlerde gördüğümüz insanlar, hepsi iyi yazılmış. Ama en iyisi hiç şüphesiz Arthur. Bu kadar kişiliği olan, karakterinin sınırları bu kadar geniş olan, hangi durumda nasıl davranacağını üç aşağı beş yukarı bilebileceğimiz, buna rağmen her iki ucada kayabilen, grinin her tonunu bünyesinde barındıran, hem sert hem yumuşak, hem esprili hem alıngan, hem gözü pek hem şüpheci olabilen kaç karakter yaratılmış sanat dünyasında emin değilim. Üstelik oyun bu muhteşem karakteri oyunun son düzlüğünde öldürüyor.

Oyunun fizik motoru harika çalışıyor. Gördüğümüz her cismin bir fiziği, o dünyada kapladığı bir alan var. Atla giderken bunların arasından geçmek, düşmemek biraz zor olsa da yine de çok tatmin edici. Tatmin edici olan bir başka şey ise combat mekaniği. Aynı şekilde bunda da düşmana veya hayvana vurduğunuzu hissediyorsunuz. Ağı çekime geçtiğinde vurduğunuz bölgenin nasıl geri sektiğini görüyorsunuz zaten. Özellikle bir açık dünya oyununda bunları yapabilmek çok çok zor. Last of Us Part 2 de böyleydi, hatta daha iyiydi ama o daha dar alanda geçen bir oyun olduğundan biraz daha kolay yapması.

Oyundaki bazı sahneler yönetmenlik ve çekim olarak da şahaneydi. Mesela colm o'driscoll'un idam sahnesi. Önce kendisinin kurtarılacağını düşündüğü için çok rahat. Ancak sonra Dutch ve ekibini görünce öleceğini anlıyor ve nefes nefese kalıyor. Üstelik ağzı kapalı olduğu için bağırıp çağıramıyor. Ölüm korkusunu nefes alış verişi ve gözleriyle mükemmel vermişler.

Bir başka etkileyici an ise alacağımızı tahsil ederken babasını gözlerinin önünde dövdüğümüz, gencin daha sonra tekrar ziyarete gittiğimizde bize bakışı. O saf nefret ve yıldırımlar saçan intikam isteğini alev alev gözlerinde görebiliyorsunuz. Çok sonraları o gence ve annesine yardım ettiğimizde Arthur'un bana teşekkür etmeyin, hayatınızı mahvettim, onuru bir yana bırakıp şu parayı alın dediği sahne çok duygusaldı. Oyunda gözlerimin yaşardığı tek andı. Bu arada o kadın ve annesi ileride golf kursu açıyormuş. Aynı kurs GTA V'te bile varmış.

Haritanın güneybatı tarafı, Meksika, çok boş geldi bana. Çok geniş ve boş bir arazi. Üstelik orada hiç yan görev veya ana görev yok. Bir iki ödül avcılığı var sadece. Biraz aceleye gelmiş gibi geldi bana.

At mekaniği inanılmaz gerçekçi. Kalçasındaki kası bile yapmışlar.

İç mekanları tasarlayan kör olmuş. Hepsi birbirinden farklı.

Daha bahsedilecek, övülecek, çok şey var. Ama yeter. Neticede muhteşem bir oyun var kaşımızda. Her yönüyle tatmin edici. Ortalamaya düştüğü tek alan bile yok.

author: DonyDoNya
text:
Главная проблема игры - утомляемость. Игра очень детальная в плане реализма. Из-за реализма всё делается медленно, топорно, неудобно - походка, поездка, перезарядка, подбирание вещей. Мне не понравилась реалистичная фишка в стрельбе с нажатием кнопки выстрела дважды для одного выстрела
Очень понравилось спокойно охотиться. В игре большое разнообразие живности разной редкости и я впервые обнаружил в себе охотничий азарт. Разное оружие под разную дичь, идеальная шкура - только выстрел в голову, выслеживание по следам и приманивание едой. Ради этого только стоит поиграть. Жаль нельзя скоротать анимацию освежевания, пусть она и приятная, но порой задалбывает
Графика в игре красивая, можно увидеть солнечные лучи проходящие сквозь стволы деревьев, следы на снегу и грязи. В такие моменты понимаешь - это любовь.
Сюжет, персонажи и диалоги - слабейшая черта игры. Не знаю что до других, но я искушённый зритель, видал много креативного. 100 процентов сюжета завершено и я ни капли не впечатлён происходящим. Потому что я понял в чём формула диалогов и основного действия. Вот вам типичные диалоги рдр2 спустя десятки часов сюжета: Артур и Хозия говорят о произошедшем "тогда" в Блэкуоттере, диалог другой миссии - Артур и Майка говорят о произошедшем в Блэкуоттере... ну вы поняли. И пока они об этом говорят обсудят очередное ограбление, чем и являются все миссии игры - бесконечные ограбления и разговоры либо об ограблениях, либо о произошедшем тогда. И долго-долго-долго ехать в каждой миссии от точки А до Б чтобы сделать очередное ограбление. При этом кататься на лошадях не так приятно как на машинах. Диалоги предсказуемые, и то что будет дальше предсказуемо, никакой интриги.
Ещё один очень большой минус игры, все согласятся - она почти полностью линейная. Казалось бы - игра добивается реалистичности и детальности во всём, игра, в которой попытались совместить всё - крафт, сурвайвал, азартные игры, пастушество, стрелялки, тамагочи. Выбора у игрока, чёрт, нет! А вот в Firewatch одна концовка, но реплики на протяжении всей игры можно выбирать и столько удовольствия от этого.
И играть приходится за подлецов тех ещё, симпатии не вызывают ни персонажи, ни главный герой Артур, который ведёт себя всегда одинаково - всем саркастично грубит.
Благо перестрелки в игре приятные и можно вдоволь повеселиться, однако механика поведения врагов в перестрелках странная. Попадаешь человеку в тело, он полсекунды тупит и дальше сражается, попадаешь в ногу - он не падает, в руку с оружием - оружие не роняет, не говоря о том, что я видел расчленёнку лишь один раз за десятки часов игры. К сожалению тут никому ничего не оторвать, если хочется. Ради этого уж лучше в Fallout New Vegas сыграть.

author: Andante
text: I was hesitant to try this game out, because of the negative reviews and the many technical issues people experienced. The version I play runs very smoothly at ultra settings and 1080p on a rtx 2060. The game itself is a masterpiece, and developers managed to create a fantastic world, simulating life in America in the late 1890s. The attention to detail is breathtaking, dialogues are rich, lively and often funny, you have the freedom to play as "good" or "bad", there are many activities and mini games you can engage with and you are also responsible for the well being of your companions and your camp. The pace of the game is slow which I really like in complete contrast to modern trends. From a technical standpoint this game looks incredible and is perhaps one of the most beautiful games I have ever played. Unfortunately the game has many bugs like suddenly crashing to desktop while on quest, which make it almost unplayable. I really hope a patch resolves this issue....Normally I would rate this with an 8 or even 9.

text:
it was released in 2019, it is 2022 and it is still a pain to play it on PC
1. I bought it on Epic and guess what, I need to use Epic launcher, then Rockstart launcher and social club, I can't just launch the game, I need all 20 launchers to be working to play in a SINGLE PLAYER game
2. They spent too much time on launchers that's why game is ALWAYS starting in windowed mode. You also can't change it in the setting from windowed to fullscreen, like, there is a button, it doesn't work. I spent a couple of hours and finally found the way to do it, you need to change Resolution without changing the mode and then magically, the mode will be set to fullscreen by itself, till the restart of the game
3. Controls and interface... I can write a doctor thesis on that one, but I will be short. They created it for consoles and gamepad, they did nothing to adjust it to pc players, nothing. It is as painful as trying to it cactus. Activate - E, take - P, take something else - TAB, interact - hold right mouse button and then press something else on a keyboard, etc. The list is indefinite. The same goes to interface and navigation in it, you can try to use mouse there, but god protect you from touching any button in the process including the mouse wheel, it will forget immediately about mouse input and will switch to something

The game looks atmospheric, a bit too much cutscenes and a bit too slow character with huge inertia, like I am controlling a huge ball and not a person with legs, a bit too much enemies and too easy shooting but it could be a good experience IF IT WAS PROPERLY SET UP FOR PC GAMING
